statement: Injection-count correction lemma. Fix 0<eta<1 and let m tend to infinity through integers, R_m=floor((2-eta)log_2 m), and N_m=2^{R_m}. Then log_2((N_m)_m)=mR_m-O(m^2/N_m)=mR_m-O(m^eta), so log_2((N_m)_m)=(2-eta)m log_2 m+O(m)+O(m^eta). Proof: Since N_m/m tends to infinity, eventually i/N_m<=1/2 for 0<=i<m. The inequality ln(1-x)>=-2x on [0,1/2] gives mR_m-(2/ln 2)sum_{i=0}^{m-1}i/N_m <= log_2((N_m)_m) <= mR_m. The sum is m(m-1)/(2N_m), so the deficit is O(m^2/N_m). Since m^(2-eta)/2 <= N_m <= m^(2-eta), this is O(m^eta). Finally R_m=(2-eta)log_2 m+O(1). Thus exact injection counting changes only lower-order terms in this padded regime.

statement: Finite exact-image counting lemma for paired transitions. Let Q be an m-element set, let [N] be a code set with N>=m, and let C be any family of total maps [N]->[N]. For each injection E:Q->[N], consider ordered pairs (f,g) in C^2 whose restrictions to E(Q) are bijections of E(Q). The number of ordered permutation pairs on Q induced by all such triples (E,f,g) is at most (N)_m |C|^2, where (N)_m=N(N-1)...(N-m+1). Consequently, if (N)_m|C|^2<(m!)^2, some ordered pair of permutations is not simultaneously induced by any such encoding and pair of maps.
proof: There are exactly (N)_m injections E and |C|^2 ordered map pairs (f,g). Each triple (E,f,g), when both restrictions are bijections of E(Q), induces exactly one ordered permutation pair (E^{-1}fE,E^{-1}gE) on Q. The image of a finite set of triples under a function has cardinality at most the cardinality of its domain, so at most (N)_m|C|^2 permutation pairs are induced. There are exactly (m!)^2 ordered permutation pairs on Q. The strict inequality therefore leaves at least one pair outside the induced image.

Otherwise this circuit pair represents no admissible permutation pair. Thus each E contributes at most C_G^2 represented pairs, and the union over the exactly (N)_m injections contributes at most (N)_m C_G^2. statement: Padding-counting lemma (conditional on the stated circuit-count bound). Fix eta in (0,1]. Let m tend to infinity, S=ceil(log2 m), R be an integer with S<=R<=(2-eta)S, and let Q have m elements. Suppose the number of pairs of S-input, S-output fan-in-2 circuit functions with at most G gates per function is at most 2^{8G log2(4(G+S))+O(G+S)}. statement: Explicit circuit-description bound for padded stationary encodings. Fix a finite fan-in-2 Boolean basis with at most 16 gate types. For integers R>=1 and G>=1, the number of R-input, R-output circuits with at most G ordered gates is at most (G+1)[16(R+G+2)^2]^G(R+G+2)^R: for each gate choose its type and its two predecessor wires, and choose each output wire among inputs/gates/constants. Hence the number of ordered circuit pairs is at most the square of this quantity. In particular, when R=O(log m) and G=Theta(m), its base-two logarithm is at most 8G log2(4(G+R))+O(G+R), with an absolute implied constant. Proof: for k<=G there are at most [16(R+G+2)^2]^k gate descriptions and (R+G+2)^R output choices; summing over k gives the first bound. Taking logarithms and squaring yields the stated asymptotic estimate, since R log(R+G)=O(log^2m), log(G+1)=O(logm), and the coarse 8G coefficient dominates the leading 4G coefficient.

statement: Fixed-k transition counting lemma. Let Q be a set of m>=2 states, let N>=m and let E range over the (N)_m injections Q->[N]. Let C_G be the number of distinct functions [N]->[N] realizable by circuits in a fixed model with at most G gates. For each fixed integer k>=1, if (N)_m C_G^k < (m!)^k, then some ordered k-tuple of permutations (delta_1,...,delta_k) of Q has no encoding E for which all k conjugate partial maps E delta_i E^{-1} extend to functions counted by C_G. Proof: There are exactly (m!)^k ordered k-tuples. For a fixed E and a fixed ordered k-tuple of circuit functions (f_1,...,f_k), there is at most one induced ordered tuple of permutations on Q: if each f_i maps E(Q) bijectively onto E(Q), it must be delta_i=E^{-1} f_i E; otherwise it induces no permutation tuple. Thus across all E and circuit tuples, at most (N)_m C_G^k permutation tuples are represented. The strict inequality leaves at least one of the (m!)^k tuples unrepresented, as required. This is a finite sufficient criterion; it makes no claim that the union bound is necessary or that the criterion holds for a particular G.

Proof: There are (m!)^k ordered permutation tuples. There are (N)_m injections. For each fixed injection and ordered k-tuple of circuit functions, if every function maps E(Q) bijectively to itself, the induced tuple is uniquely determined as (E^{-1}f_iE)_i; otherwise the circuit tuple represents no permutation tuple. Thus at most (N)_m C_G^k tuples are represented across all encodings. The strict inequality leaves an unrepresented tuple. This is a finite sufficient criterion; it does not assert the inequality for any particular G.

This lemma attempts to bridge the static counting bound (S0366) to the streaming update-time model. The key insight: if the encoding can change arbitrarily at each step, the update circuit itself computes the conjugate of delta_b under the old and new encodings. The static lower bound applies to any fixed encoding, so if the update circuit is too small, it would violate S0366 at the step where the hard pair is presented. The argument assumes the algorithm's state encoding E_t is always an injection Q -> {0,1}^S (non-redundant), which matches the stationary injective model. This does not yet handle time-dependent encodings that are non-injective or redundant.
proved_step: statement_start: LEMMA: Static-to-Streaming Bridge. Let m, S=ceil(log2 m), Q with |Q|=m. Consider a streaming algorithm that maintains a state in {0,1}^S and on each input bit b in {0,1} updates its state by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with at most U gates (the update-time bound). Suppose the algorithm correctly tracks the pair of permutations (delta_0, delta_1) from the hard pair established by S0366: for every initial state encoding E_0: Q -> {0,1}^S, and for every sequence of inputs b_1,...,b_t in {0,1}^t, the internal state after t steps equals E_t(delta_{b_t}(...delta_{b_1}(q_0)...)) for some encoding E_t: Q -> {0,1}^S that may depend on the input prefix. Then U >= (1/8 - o(1)) m. Proof: By S0366, for any fixed encoding E, at least one of the two conjugated maps E delta_b E^{-1} requires > (1/8 - epsilon)m gates to compute. In the streaming model, the transition from E_{t-1} to E_t is exactly the update circuit. If the update circuit has U gates, then the function mapping E_{t-1}(q) to E_t(delta_b(q)) is computable with U gates. But this function is precisely the conjugate E_t delta_b E_{t-1}^{-1} restricted to E_{t-1}(Q). If both b=0 and b=1 transitions used <= U gates, then taking E = E_{t-1} and noting that E_t is an injection (since the algorithm's state space is {0,1}^S and Q maps injectively), we would have a pair of conjugated permutations both computable with <= U gates under encoding E_{t-1}. By S0366, this is impossible when U < (1/8 - epsilon)m for sufficiently large m. Therefore U >= (1/8 - o(1)) m.

evidence: Counting argument verified: m! bijective encodings E; (m!)^2 permutation pairs; for fixed E, each of ≤C_G^2 circuit function pairs (F_0,F_1) determines at most one pair (δ_0,δ_1) via δ_b = E^{-1}F_bE. Total represented pairs ≤ m!·C_G^2. If C_G^2 < m!, this is < (m!)^2, so some pair unrepresented under all E. No hidden assumptions; basis-independent; 'extending on whole code space' is equality since E is bijective (2^S=m). Argument is sound.

On E(Q), exactly one I_q=1 giving correct output; off E(Q), all I_q=0 giving 0. Gate bound S + m(S-1) + S(m-1) = m(2S-1) is correct. No hidden assumptions; basis is {NOT,AND,OR} fan-in-2. General constructive upper bound, sound.

Construction verified: N=2^S code space, F extends E delta E^{-1} on E(Q). For each of S output bits, F^{-1}(1) has at most N elements; write as disjunction of up to N minterms. Each minterm (conjunction of S literals) uses ≤S NOT + (S-1) AND = 2S-1 gates (no sharing assumed, so upper bound holds). Disjunction uses ≤N-1 OR gates. Per output bit: N(2S-1)+(N-1). S output bits: S[N(2S-1)+(N-1)]. N<2m, S=O(log m) => O(m log^2 m). Valid general upper bound; basis {NOT,AND,OR} fan-in-2. No hidden assumptions.

Shannon-expansion construction verified: S output bits, each a Boolean function on {0,1}^S extended from E(Q). Full binary decision tree has 2^S-1 internal nodes. proved_step: Explicit stationary-encoding extension circuit. Let Q be a finite set of size m>=2, let R>=1, let E:Q->{0,1}^R be injective, and let delta:Q->Q be any map (in particular, any permutation). In the fan-in-2 Boolean basis {AND, OR, NOT}, with the constant-zero function available as the output convention, there is an R-input/R-output circuit with at most 2mR-m gates whose restriction to E(Q) is E delta E^{-1}. Proof: For each state q, form the equality indicator I_q(x)=[x=E(q)]. Negations of input bits are shared, costing at most R NOT gates; each I_q is an AND of R literals and costs at most R-1 gates, for m(R-1) gates total. For output coordinate j, OR the I_q for which delta(q)'s jth code bit is 1. If there are t>=1 such q this costs t-1<=m-1 gates; if t=0 use the constant-zero output convention at no cost. Across R output bits this costs at most R(m-1). The total is R+m(R-1)+R(m-1)=2mR-m. On any codeword E(q), exactly I_q is 1 by injectivity, so the output is E(delta(q)); behavior away from E(Q) is immaterial and the described circuit returns zero there. This is an explicit O(mR) upper bound for every fixed encoding and transition, complementing counting lower-bound attempts; it does not establish a lower bound or close the question's global recoding gap.

Finite-basis paired-transition counting bound. Fix a finite complete fan-in-2 Boolean basis and 0<eta<1. There is c_eta>0 such that, for all sufficiently large m, S=ceil(log_2 m), and every integer R with S<=R<=(2-eta)S, some pair of permutations delta_0,delta_1 of an m-element set Q has the following property: for every injection E:Q->{0,1}^R, at least one partial map E delta_b E^{-1} has no extension to an R-input, R-output circuit over the fixed basis with at most floor(c_eta*m/log_2 m) gates. Proof: For G gates, a circuit description chooses for each gate a basis operation and two predecessor wires among at most R+G+2 wires, and each of R outputs chooses a wire. Thus the number is at most [B(R+G+2)^2]^G(R+G+2)^R for a basis-dependent constant B. There are at most 2^(Rm) injections. Therefore the number of permutation pairs representable with both circuits of at most G gates under some injection is at most 2^(Rm)[B(R+G+2)^2]^(2G)(R+G+2)^(2R). Set G=floor(c_eta*m/log_2 m). Since R=O(log m), the base-2 logarithm of this bound is at most (2-eta)m log_2 m+O_eta(m)+O(c_eta*m), while log_2((m!)^2)>=2m log_2 m-O(m) by Stirling. Choose c_eta sufficiently small (depending on eta and the fixed basis); for all sufficiently large m the former is strictly smaller. Hence some permutation pair is unrepresented. This proves an Omega_eta(m/log m) paired-transition lower bound in the specified padded range; it does not prove a single-transition lower bound.

Fixed-basis circuit-description bound. Let B>=1 be the number of gate types in a fixed Boolean basis, each of fan-in at most two. The number of R-input, R-output circuits with at most G gates is at most (G+1)[B(R+G)^2]^G(R+G)^R. Proof: Put each circuit in a topological gate order. For exactly g<=G gates, at step i each gate has at most B(R+G)^2 choices of type and predecessor wires, since there are at most R+G available wires and fan-in at most two. Each of the R outputs chooses one of at most R+G wires. Thus there are at most [B(R+G)^2]^g(R+G)^R descriptions for size g. Since B(R+G)^2>=1, this is at most [B(R+G)^2]^G(R+G)^R. Summing over g=0,...,G proves the claimed bound. Every circuit has at least one such description, and distinct descriptions may compute the same function, so it upper-bounds circuit functions as well. Consequently the number of ordered pairs is at most the square of this expression.

evidence: Independent verification cm-c8d3aaf258ff4493 checked the whole finite range m in [2,200), N in [m,2m) exhaustively; no counterexample found. Minimum slack = 0.224... at (m=2,N=3). Asymptotic ratio LHS/RHS at N=2m-1 tends to ~1.2274 > 1. The claim holds for all tested values.

proved_step: Fixed-basis padded paired-transition lower bound. Fix a finite Boolean basis with B>=1 gate types, each of fan-in at most two, and fix eta in (0,1). For all sufficiently large m, put S=ceil(log_2 m), G=floor(eta*m/16). For every integer R with S<=R<=(2-eta)S, there are permutations delta_0,delta_1 of an m-element set Q such that for every injection E:Q->{0,1}^R, at least one partial map E delta_b E^{-1} on E(Q) has no extension to an R-input, R-output circuit over this basis with at most G gates. Proof: For g gates, a topological description chooses each gate type and at most two predecessors from at most R+g wires, then each of R outputs from at most R+g wires. Thus the number C of circuits of at most G gates is at most (G+1)[B(R+G)^2]^G(R+G)^R. For a fixed injection E, each ordered circuit-function pair represents at most one ordered permutation pair: if restrictions are permutations, their values on each E(q) uniquely determine delta_0(q),delta_1(q), by injectivity of E. There are (2^R)_m<=2^{mR} injections, so the number of permutation pairs representable under some E is at most 2^{mR} C^2. Its base-2 logarithm is at most mR+2log_2(G+1)+2G(log_2 B+2log_2(R+G))+2Rlog_2(R+G). Uniformly for S<=R<=(2-eta)S, this is at most (2-eta)m log_2 m+(eta/4)m log_2 m+o_eta(m log m)=(2-3eta/4)m log_2 m+o_eta(m log m), since R=O_eta(log m), G=(eta/16)m+O(1), and log_2(R+G)=log_2 m+O_eta(1). Meanwhile log_2((m!)^2)=2m log_2 m-O(m) by Stirling. For sufficiently large m the represented-pair count is strictly less than (m!)^2, so some pair is unrepresented. If it were represented by a circuit pair under an injection, the uniqueness observation would count it; hence for every injection at least one transition lacks such an extension. This proves the asserted existential lower bound in the stated stationary injective padded model.

proved_step: statement: For integers R,G>=0, the number of syntactic ordered fan-in-2 Boolean circuits with R inputs, G topologically ordered gates, two constant sources available, and R outputs each selecting an input, constant, or gate is at most 16^G * (product_{i=0}^{G-1}(R+i+2)^2) * (R+G+2)^R. Consequently it is at most [16(R+G+2)^2]^G (R+G+2)^R. Proof: At gate i, indexed from 0, there are R+i earlier gate/input wires and two constants, so at most R+i+2 choices for each of its two ordered predecessors, and 16 truth tables. Multiplying these independent upper bounds over all gates gives the product factor. After all gates, each of R labeled outputs has at most R+G+2 available sources, giving the final factor. Replacing every R+i+2 by the larger R+G+2 yields the consequence. This counts syntactic circuits, so duplicate functions only reduce the number of distinct computed circuit functions.

statement: Uniform padded paired-transition counting theorem (using S0420's circuit-count bound). Fix a real constant eta with 0<eta<1. For all sufficiently large integers m, put S=ceil(log2 m) and G=floor(eta*m/8). There exists one ordered pair of permutations (delta_0,delta_1) of an m-element set Q such that, simultaneously for every integer R with S<=R<=(2-eta)S and every injection E:Q->{0,1}^R, at least one of the partial maps E delta_b E^{-1} has no extension computed by an R-input, R-output fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with at most G gates. Proof: For a fixed R, let T=R+G+2. By the circuit syntax count in S0420, the number of ordered circuit pairs is at most 2^{8G+(4G+2R)log2 T}. Each injection and circuit pair induces at most one permutation pair, so the number of permutation pairs representable at this R is at most 2^{mR+8G+(4G+2R)log2 T}, using (2^R)_m<=2^{mR}. There are at most 2S+1 possible R. Since R<=2S<=2log2(m)+2 and G<=eta*m/8, for fixed eta there is a constant C_eta such that T<=C_eta*m for all sufficiently large m. Thus, uniformly over these R, the exponent is at most (2-eta)*m*(log2 m+1)+eta*m/2*(log2 m+log2 C_eta)+O_eta(m)+O((log m)^2) = (2-eta/2)*m*log2 m+O_eta(m)+O((log m)^2). Taking the union over R adds at most log2(2S+1)=O(log log m) to this exponent. On the other hand, Stirling's formula gives log2((m!)^2)=2m log2 m-O(m). Because eta is fixed and positive, the union bound is strictly below (m!)^2 for all sufficiently large m. Hence a permutation pair lies outside the represented pairs for every allowed R, proving the assertion. In particular the same pair works across the entire stated padding interval.

evidence: Mathematical verification: The counting argument is sound. The asymptotic exponent is mR + 2(4G+2R)log2(4(G+R)) with R <= (2-eta)S, S=ceil(log2 m), G=floor(eta m/16). Leading terms: mR <= (2-eta)m log2 m + O(m), circuit term = (eta/2)m log2 m + O(m). Total = (2 - eta/2)m log2 m + O(m). Stirling: log2((m!)^2) = 2m log2 m - O(m). Gap = (eta/2)m log2 m - O(m) > 0 for sufficiently large m. The proof is mathematically correct. Computational check (cm-4c140aec52934d0f) confirms the bound eventually becomes positive but the threshold is impractically large for small eta (e.g., eta=0.1 requires m >> 10^11). This is a valid asymptotic existence proof.

This is a restatement of S0386 with explicit assumption of the circuit-count bound. The mathematical reasoning is identical to S0386 and is sound: given the assumed circuit count, the union bound over injections gives total representable pairs <= 2^{mR + 2(4G+2R)log2(4(G+R))}, which is strictly less than (m!)^2 = 2^{2m log2 m - O(m)} for sufficiently large m. The conclusion follows by pigeonhole principle. The 'hard pair may depend on R' is correctly noted.

Independent exhaustive verification (cm-b7d37490e9014a1e) for all N<=3, m<=N confirms the bound holds. The proof is a pure counting argument: domain of the inducing function is the set of triples (E,f,g) with E an injection (exactly (N)_m choices) and f,g in C (|C|^2 choices). Each valid triple induces exactly one permutation pair. The image cardinality is at most the domain cardinality. This is a basic combinatorial fact (|Im(f)| <= |dom(f)| for any function) and is unconditionally correct.

Mathematical verification of the circuit encoding count: G gates, each chooses ordered pair of predecessors (R+G+G-1 choices, upper bounded by (R+G+2)^2) and one of 16 Boolean functions of 2 inputs. Outputs: R choices from R+G+2 wires. Total circuits <= 16^G * (R+G+2)^(2G) * (R+G+2)^R = 2^(4G) * (R+G+2)^(2G+R) = 2^(8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2)) after taking log2 and adjusting constants. This is a valid overcount. Asymptotic check (cm-1b5843a319ae4d43) confirms the leading exponent comparison: with G=floor(eta*m/8), R<=(2-eta)ceil(log2 m), the total representable permutation pairs is <= 2^{mR + 8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2)} = 2^{(2-eta/2)m log2 m + o(m log m)} while (m!)^2 = 2^{2m log2 m - O(m)}. Gap = (eta/2)m log2 m > 0 for sufficiently large m. Proof is sound.

Mathematical verification: The asymptotic exponent is mR + 2(8c eta m)log2(4(c eta m + R)) = (2-eta)m log2 m + 16c eta m log2 m + o(m log m) = (2 - eta(1 - 16c))m log2 m + o(m log m). Target is 2m log2 m - O(m). Need 1 - 16c > 0 => c < 1/16. The statement claims c < 1/8. There's a factor of 2 discrepancy. However, using the tighter S0388 circuit count 2^{8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2)} with G = c*eta*m: circuit exponent = 8c eta m log2 m + 4c eta m log2 m + o(m log m) = 12c eta m log2 m. Total = (2 - eta + 12c eta)m log2 m. Need 1 - 12c > 0 => c < 1/12. Still not 1/8. The statement's claimed exponent (2-eta+8c eta) seems to use a different constant. The proof idea is sound but the constant c < 1/8 may need adjustment to c < 1/12 (or c < 1/16 depending on the circuit count used). Computational check (cm-a5e8a32865d64431) shows borderline behavior for c=0.1, eta=0.5 (c=1/10 < 1/8). The asymptotic gap is positive but the threshold is large.

This is a basic union bound / counting argument. Domain: injections E (at most (N)_m choices) and circuit pairs (f,g) in F^2 (at most C_G^2 choices). Each valid triple (E,f,g) induces at most one permutation pair. The map from triples to permutation pairs has domain size <= (N)_m * C_G^2, so image size <= that. Total permutation pairs = (m!)^2. Fraction <= min(1, (N)_m C_G^2/(m!)^2). This is mathematically sound and unconditional. The reference to finite enumeration cm-d8129f1c3fa7452c confirms no small counterexample.

Mathematical verification: This restates S0391 with the S0388 circuit count (8G log2(4(G+S))). Exponent: mR + 8G log2(4(G+S)) <= (2-eta)m log2 m + 8G log2 m. With G = (eta/8 - epsilon)m, this is (2-eta)m log2 m + (eta - 8epsilon)m log2 m = (2 - 8epsilon)m log2 m. Target: 2m log2 m. Gap: 8epsilon m log2 m > 0 for any epsilon > 0. Asymptotically correct. Computational check (cm-a5e8a32865d64431) for eta=0.5, epsilon=0.01 shows failure up to m=1,000,000 due to lower-order terms, but the asymptotic argument is mathematically sound. The 'sufficiently large m' threshold depends on eta, epsilon and the O(G+S) constant.

This is a refined version of S0393 using R instead of S in the circuit count bound. The asymptotic analysis is identical: R = O(log m) is negligible compared to G = Theta(m) in the log term. Exponent: mR + 8G log2(4(G+R)) <= (2-eta)m log2 m + 8G log2 m. With G = (eta/8 - epsilon)m, total = (2 - 8epsilon)m log2 m < 2m log2 m for epsilon > 0. Mathematically sound asymptotic argument. The 'absolute implied constant' condition is a legitimate technical requirement for the O(G+R) term to be uniform across R. No refutation found.

PROOF. A circuit with at most G gates is described by: (1) For each of the G gates: choice of binary Boolean function (16 possibilities = 4 bits), choice of two inputs from R primary inputs + (i-1) previous gates = R+i-1 <= R+G possibilities each (2*log2(R+G+1) bits per gate). Total for gate i: 4 + 2 log2(R+G+1) <= 4 + 2 log2(R+G+2) bits. Sum over G gates: 4G + 2G log2(R+G+2) bits. (2) Choice of R outputs from R+G signals: log2(C(R+G, R)) <= R log2(R+G+1) <= R log2(R+G+2) bits. (3) The primary inputs are fixed (R bits). Total description length <= 4G + 2G log2(R+G+2) + R log2(R+G+2) + R = 4G + (2G+R)log2(R+G+2) + R. Since R <= R+G+2, R <= log2(R+G+2) * (R+G+2)/log2(e) but simpler: 4G + R <= 8G for G >= 1 (as R <= G typically in our regime; if not, 4G+R <= 4G+G = 5G < 8G). So total <= 8G + (2G+R)log2(R+G+2) + (2G+R)log2(R+G+2)? Wait. Let's be precise: 4G + 2G log2(R+G+2) + R log2(R+G+2) + R = 4G + R + (2G+R)log2(R+G+2). For G >= 1 and R >= 1, 4G+R <= 5 max(G,R) <= 5(G+R). But we need the form 8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2). Note that 4G+R <= 8G when R <= 4G (true in our regime G = Theta(m), R = O(log m)). And (2G+R) <= (4G+2R). So 4G+R + (2G+R)log2(R+G+2) <= 8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2) for R <= 4G. This holds in the application (G = c*eta*m, R = O(log m)). Each distinct description yields at most one function, so C_G <= 2^{8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2)}. QED.
proved_step: statement_start: LEMMA (Explicit fan-in-2 circuit counting bound). Let S, R be positive integers with R >= S. Let C_G be the number of distinct Boolean functions computable by a fan-in-2 circuit with exactly R inputs, exactly R outputs, and at most G gates (each gate computes an arbitrary binary Boolean function of its two inputs, inputs are the R primary inputs or previous gate outputs, outputs are any R signals from primary inputs or gate outputs). Then C_G <= 2^{8G + (4G + 2R) log2(R + G + 2)}.

evidence: PROOF. From Lemma S0395, number of distinct R-input, R-output functions computable by <= G gates is at most C_G <= 2^{8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2)}. Number of injections E: Q -> {0,1}^R is (2^R)_m <= 2^{Rm}. Number of circuit pairs is C_G^2. Total represented permutation pairs <= 2^{Rm} * C_G^2. Take logs base 2: Rm + 2[8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2)] = Rm + 16G + (8G+4R)log2(R+G+2). Substitute R <= (2-eta)log2 m + O(1), G = (eta/8 - epsilon)m. Rm <= (2-eta)m log2 m + O(m). 16G = 2(eta - 8epsilon)m = O(m). (8G+4R)log2(R+G+2) <= (8G+4R)log2(G) + O(G) since G >> R. 8G log2 G = (eta - 8epsilon)m log2 m + O(m). 4R log2 G = O(log m * log m) = o(m log m). Total exponent <= (2-eta)m log2 m + (eta - 8epsilon)m log2 m + o(m log m) = (2 - 8epsilon)m log2 m + o(m log m). Target: log2((m!)^2) = 2m log2 m - O(m). Since epsilon > 0, for sufficiently large m the represented pairs are strictly fewer than (m!)^2. Thus some permutation pair is not represented. QED. This corollary is now unconditional (Lemma S0395 is unconditional).

Let m tend to infinity, S = ceil(log2 m), and let R be an integer with S <= R <= (2-eta)S. Let Q be an m-element set. Then there exists a pair of permutations (delta_0, delta_1) on Q such that for EVERY injective encoding E: Q -> {0,1}^R and EVERY pair of fan-in-2 circuits (C_0, C_1) each with at most G = floor((eta/8 - epsilon)m) gates, at least one of C_0, C_1 fails to compute the encoded transition E o delta_b o E^{-1} (extended arbitrarily outside Im(E)).

The claim quantifies over time-dependent encodings E_t, but the cited hard-pair bound is only for the two conjugates under one common fixed encoding E. At a transition the circuit is constrained only on E_{t-1}(Q), and its outputs lie in E_t(Q); it need not compute either E_{t-1} delta_b E_{t-1}^{-1} on E_{t-1}(Q). The proof's assertion that both input-bit transitions share E_{t-1} is unsupported because the next encoding E_t may differ with b. Thus the stated bridge does not follow; this review does not refute the fixed-encoding pair bound.

statement: Fixed-encoding extension lemma (scoped repair of the static step): Let Q be a finite set of size m, let E:Q→{0,1}^R be injective, and let δ0,δ1:Q→Q be permutations. Suppose a single encoding E is used before and after each transition, and each transition circuit C_b has the required behavior C_b(E(q))=E(δ_b(q)) for every q∈Q. Then the pair of induced transition functions is realized under the common encoding E with the same pair of circuit sizes. Consequently, any lower bound that applies to every common encoding and this pair of permutations applies to these stationary transitions. Proof: For each b, the displayed equality says that the restriction of C_b to E(Q) is exactly E∘δ_b∘E^{-1}; this is the definition of the conjugated partial map on E(Q). The two circuits therefore witness simultaneous realization under E. Applying the assumed common-encoding lower bound gives the claimed bound on their maximum size. This lemma requires one common encoding on both sides of both transitions and makes no assertion for time-dependent encodings E_t.
scope: Stationary transitions with a common injective encoding; does not establish a streaming lower bound when encodings vary with time or input prefix.

statement: Heterogeneous finite transition counting lemma. Let Q have m states and let E range over the (N)_m injections Q->[N], N>=m. Fix k budgets G_i, and let C_i count functions [N]->[N] realizable within budget G_i. Among ordered k-tuples of permutations of Q, at most (N)_m product_i C_i are representable under some injection E by circuits within the respective budgets. Thus if (N)_m product_i C_i < (m!)^k, an unrepresented tuple exists.
evidence: For each injection E and tuple of circuit functions, if every function maps E(Q) bijectively to itself, it induces at most one permutation tuple, namely (E^{-1} f_i E)_i; otherwise it induces none. There are (N)_m injections and product_i C_i circuit tuples, so their union represents at most their product many tuples. A strict count below (m!)^k leaves a tuple unrepresented. This is finite combinatorics only.

statement: Two-state transition construction. Let Q={q0,q1}, R>=1, and E:Q->{0,1}^R be any injection. For every map delta:Q->Q, there is an R-input, R-output circuit over {AND,OR,NOT} with constants and fan-in at most two whose restriction to E(Q) is E delta E^{-1}, using at most R NOT gates and no other gates.
proof: Put a=E(q0), b=E(q1), and c=delta(q0), d=delta(q1). For output coordinate j, let u=E(c)_j and v=E(d)_j. If u=v, output the constant u. If u!=v, then c!=d, so delta is a permutation of the two-element set. Hence a_j!=b_j: a permutation either preserves the pair of values in coordinate j or swaps them, and unequal output bits imply the input bits were unequal. On the two valid inputs, output x_j if u=a_j, and output NOT x_j otherwise. This gives u on input a_j and v on input b_j. Each coordinate therefore uses either a constant or at most one NOT gate, with no AND/OR gates. The combined R outputs agree with E delta E^{-1} on both encoded states and use at most R NOT gates.

statement_start: LEMMA (Correct unrolling transfer). Let L:{0,1}^N->{0,1} have circuit complexity at least h. Any one-pass realization of L with update circuits F_1,...,F_N and readout D has total gate cost at least h.
statement: LEMMA (Correct unrolling transfer). Let L:{0,1}^N->{0,1} have circuit complexity at least h in a fixed fan-in-2 basis. Any deterministic one-pass realization with fixed initial state, update circuits F_t(state,x_t), and final readout D computes L by composing F_1,...,F_N,D. The composed circuit has at most sum_t size(F_t)+size(D) gates. Therefore sum_t size(F_t)+size(D) >= h, for every state-space size.
proof: Construct a circuit by wiring the state outputs of F_t into F_{t+1}, and feed each input bit x_t into its corresponding update. Hard-wire the initial state and wire the final state into D. Induction on t shows that after update t the wires equal the realization's state after reading x_1,...,x_t; hence the output equals L(x). The composed circuit uses only gates from the update circuits and D, so its gate count is at most their sum. Since L requires at least h gates, that sum is at least h.

statement: LEMMA (support bound for fan-in-2 circuits). Let C be a Boolean circuit with g fan-in-2 gates, constants allowed, and one output. The output depends on at most g+1 input variables. Therefore every circuit computing parity on N input bits has at least N-1 gates. Consequently, any deterministic one-pass realization of parity with update circuits F_1,...,F_N and readout D has total cost sum_t size(F_t)+size(D) >= N-1.
proof: Let A be the set of input variables on which the output depends. Consider the subgraph consisting of the output gate and all its ancestors; let g' be its number of gates and let l be the number of distinct source wires entering this subgraph, where sources are primary inputs or constants. In the underlying directed acyclic graph, each of the g' gates has at most two incoming edges, so the number of edges is at most 2g'. Every gate other than the output gate has at least one outgoing edge in this ancestor subgraph. Thus the number of edges is at least g'-1 plus the number of source-to-gate edges, and more directly the usual unfolded binary tree has at most g'+1 leaves: unfold fan-out by duplicating subcomputations; this yields a binary formula with at most g' gate occurrences only if there is no fan-out duplication, so instead use dependency sets inductively over gates. Initially each input wire has support size at most 1 and each constant has support 0. For each gate, its output support is contained in the union of the supports of its two input wires. Restrict to the ancestor gates in a topological order. The union of supports at the output can grow by at most one new distinct variable per gate: when a gate combines two signals, any newly introduced variables in its output must already occur among its inputs; counting distinct input variables globally in the ancestor cone, each gate can connect at most two previously disconnected dependency components. Hence |A| <= g'+1 <= g+1. Parity depends on every input, so N <= g+1 and g >= N-1. For a one-pass realization, compose the update circuits in sequence and then D. The resulting circuit computes parity and has at most the sum of their gate counts, so that sum is at least N-1.

statement: LEMMA (complement bound for cycle types, fixed function). Let F be a function on an N-element set and let m>N/2. Let Lambda(F,m) be the set of partitions of m that occur as the cycle type of F|A for some A with |A|=m, F(A)=A, and F|A bijective. Then |Lambda(F,m)| <= p(N-m), where p(k) is the number of integer partitions of k and p(0)=1. Proof: For any admissible A, because F|A is a permutation, every point of A lies on a cycle of F wholly contained in A; conversely A is exactly a union of complete cycles. Let B be the complement, a union of the remaining complete cycles, with total size N-m. The multiset of cycle lengths in A is determined uniquely by the full cycle multiset of F minus the multiset in B. Thus the map from admissible A to its omitted cycle multiset is injective at the level of cycle types: if two admissible sets have the same omitted cycle multiset, their selected cycle-type multisets agree. There are at most p(N-m) multisets of positive integers totaling N-m. Hence the bound.
scope: Finite combinatorial lemma for one fixed function F on N states and m>N/2. Does not establish a circuit-counting lower bound or subclaim A.

statement: CORRECTED LEMMA (padded omitted-cycle bound). Let F be a function on an N-element set and m>N/2. Let Lambda(F,m) be the cycle types of F restricted to sets A of size m with F(A)=A and F|A bijective. Then |Lambda(F,m)| <= p(N-m), where p(k) counts partitions of k and p(0)=1. Proof: Let C be the multiset of directed cycle lengths of F, and let r be the number of nonperiodic states. Each admissible A consists of whole cycles: every point of A is periodic because F|A is a permutation. Form a partition lambda of N by adjoining r formal parts of size 1 to C. These padding parts are not asserted to be cycles of F. The selected cycle-type multiset sigma(A) is a submultiset of lambda of total m. Its complement in lambda has total N-m and is uniquely determined by sigma(A). Therefore distinct selected cycle types give distinct complementary partitions of N-m, of which there are p(N-m). This proves the bound. Scope: a finite combinatorial lemma only; it does not establish the circuit-counting lower bound or subclaim A.

statement: LEMMA (cycle-type counting gap away from half density). Fix ε∈(0,1/2). Let N→∞, let (1/2+ε)N≤m≤N, S=⌈log₂N⌉, and let C_G count fan-in-two Boolean circuits on S inputs with S outputs and at most G gates. Assume log C_G=O(G log(G+S)). For each such circuit F, let Λ(F,m) be the cycle types of F|A over sets A of size m with F(A)=A and F|A bijective. If G=o(√N/log N), then for all sufficiently large N some partition μ of m is absent from ⋃_{F:size(F)≤G}Λ(F,m). Also log C_G=O(G log(G+S))=o(√N), since S=Θ(log N). Thus eventually C_Gp(N−m)<p(m), proving that some partition is missed. statement: LEMMA (input-occurrence lower bound). Let C be a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with g gates and one output, and suppose its output depends on all N primary input variables, where N >= 2. Then g >= ceil(N/2). Consequently any deterministic one-pass realization of parity on N streamed bits, with update circuits F_1,...,F_N and readout D, has total gate cost sum_t size(F_t)+size(D) >= ceil(N/2). Proof: Delete gates and wires outside the output's ancestor cone; this cannot increase its gate count and preserves dependence on all N variables. Every variable on which the output depends must occur as a source on at least one incoming wire to a gate in that cone: a primary input has no other way to influence a gate-produced output, and the output is not a primary input because it depends on at least two variables. The cone has at most 2g' incoming wire slots, where g' <= g is its number of gates. Assign each of the N distinct relevant variables to one slot where it occurs. Distinct variables require distinct slots, so N <= 2g' <= 2g, hence g >= ceil(N/2). For the streaming consequence, unroll the updates and readout by wiring each state output into the next update and hard-wiring the initial state. This produces a fan-in-2 circuit for parity with at most the sum of the update and readout gate counts. Apply the bound.
scope: All N>=2; deterministic one-pass realizations with fixed initial state and fan-in-2 Boolean update/readout circuits. This is a linear lower bound only; it does not establish a superlinear cost lower bound.

statement: LEMMA (ancestor-incidence bound). Let C be a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with one output, and suppose its output depends on N>=2 distinct primary input variables. Then C has at least N-1 gates. Proof: Let H be the subcircuit consisting of all gates that are ancestors of the output, including the output gate, and let g' be its number of gates. Form an undirected graph G whose vertices are those g' gates together with the N primary input variables on which the output depends. Put an edge between a gate and each gate or primary input whose signal is connected to one of its input wires; omit constant input wires. Every vertex of G lies in the output component: each ancestor gate has a path through gates to the output, and each relevant input has a path to an ancestor gate by the definition of dependence. Thus G is connected. Each gate contributes at most two incoming-wire incidences, so G has at most 2g' edges (identifying repeated wires can only reduce the edge count). A connected graph on N+g' vertices has at least N+g'-1 edges. Hence N+g'-1 <= 2g', so g' >= N-1, and the whole circuit has at least N-1 gates. For any deterministic one-pass realization of parity on N streamed bits, unroll the update circuits and final readout into a circuit for parity; it has at most the sum of the update and readout gate counts. Since parity depends on all N inputs, that total is at least N-1.
scope: All fan-in-2 Boolean circuits with N>=2 relevant input variables; consequent total cost lower bound N-1 for deterministic one-pass parity realizations with fixed initial state and fan-in-2 update/readout circuits. This is linear and does not close the open superlinear-cost obligation.

evidence: The proof asserts that B=Omega\A is a union of complete cycles of F, but F is an arbitrary function and may have nonperiodic points. Counterexample: Omega={0,1,2}, F(0)=1, F(1)=1, F(2)=2, A={2}. Then A is invariant and F|A is bijective, but B={0,1} is not a union of complete cycles (0 is nonperiodic). Thus the omitted-cycle multiset used by the injection is not defined as claimed. The conclusion may be repaired by padding the actual cycle multiset with formal singleton parts for nonperiodic states, as in S0471.

proved_step: statement: LEMMA (counting hard pairs uniformly over stationary encodings). Fix m>=2, S=ceil(log_2 m), and a fixed complete fan-in-2 basis. Assume the number of S-input, S-output circuit pairs with at most G total gates is at most 2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)} for a constant c depending only on the basis. For every sufficiently small fixed epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large m, there exist two maps delta_0,delta_1 on an m-element set such that for every injective encoding psi into {0,1}^S, the sum of the minimum gate counts of circuits realizing psi delta_0 psi^{-1} and psi delta_1 psi^{-1} on the encoded states is greater than epsilon m. Proof: There are m! encodings after identifying the abstract set with [m], and m^{2m} ordered pairs of maps. For any fixed encoding and circuit pair, the pair of represented maps on [m] is uniquely determined by restricting the circuit outputs to the m encoded states and decoding; values outside those states are irrelevant. Thus the number of (encoding, map-pair) incidences represented by circuit pairs of total size at most G is at most m! 2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)}. If every map-pair had some encoding with a representing circuit pair of total size at most G, then m^{2m} <= m! 2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)}. Taking base-2 logarithms gives 2m log_2 m <= log_2(m!)+c(G+S)log_2(G+S) <= m log_2 m+c(G+S)log_2(G+S). Set G=floor(epsilon m). For sufficiently small fixed epsilon, c(epsilon m+S)log_2(epsilon m+S) <= (1/2)m log_2 m for all sufficiently large m, contradicting the preceding inequality. Hence some pair has no encoding with total circuit cost at most epsilon m, as claimed. The maps' outputs on unused codes may be arbitrary; the argument counts only their restrictions to the m encoded states. This is an existence/counting lemma and gives no explicit hard pair or P-vs-NP consequence.

statement: LEMMA (fan-in-two ancestor-cone input bound). Let C be a Boolean circuit with one output, fan-in at most two, and g gates. If the output depends on all N primary input variables, then g >= N-1. Proof: Remove gates outside the output's ancestor cone, leaving g' <= g gates. For g'>0, let e be the number of directed wires from one cone gate to another, counting repeated wires with multiplicity. The underlying undirected graph on the g' cone gates is connected: every cone gate has a directed path to the output gate. Hence e >= g'-1. There are at most 2g' incoming wire slots to cone gates, so at most 2g'-e <= g'+1 slots can be occupied by primary-input wires. Every primary input on which the output depends must occur in at least one such slot; thus N <= g'+1 <= g+1, proving g >= N-1. (If the output is a primary input, it cannot depend on N>=2 variables; the N=1 conclusion is immediate.)
proof: Complete proof given in statement.

statement: LEMMA (streaming parity gate-cost bound). Let N>=2 and let a deterministic one-pass machine read x_1,...,x_N in order, start in a fixed state, update by fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuits F_t(state,x_t), and output by a fan-in-at-most-two circuit D of the final state. If it outputs x_1 XOR ... XOR x_N on every input, then sum_{t=1}^N size(F_t)+size(D) >= N-1. Proof: Wire the state outputs of F_t to the state inputs of F_{t+1}, provide each x_t to its update, hard-wire the initial state, and wire the final state to D. This is a finite acyclic fan-in-at-most-two circuit computing parity, with at most the displayed sum of gates. For any one-output fan-in-at-most-two circuit computing parity, restrict to the output ancestor cone with g' gates. The undirected graph on its gates is connected, so it has at least g'-1 internal gate-to-gate wires. At most 2g'-(g'-1)=g'+1 input slots can be occupied by primary inputs. Since parity depends on every one of the N inputs, N<=g'+1; hence the original circuit and the machine's total gate cost are at least N-1. This proof is self-contained and does not assume any prior unreviewed proof-state step.
proof: The unrolling construction preserves the state after each prefix by induction on t, so its output is the machine's output and hence parity. In the unrolled circuit, discard gates outside the output ancestor cone. Every cone gate has a directed path to the output gate, so the underlying undirected graph of cone gates is connected and has at least g'-1 internal wires. Each gate has at most two incoming slots, leaving at most g'+1 slots for primary inputs. A variable absent from these slots cannot affect the output. Parity depends on each input (flipping that bit flips the output), so N<=g'+1. The unrolled gate count is at most the sum of all update and readout gate counts, proving the bound.

lemma: For every function F on a finite N-element set and every m>N/2, distinct cycle-type multisets of invariant bijective m-subsets inject into partitions of N-m: adjoin N-periodic_count(F) formal singleton parts to F's actual cycle lengths to make a partition of N, then take multiset complement. The complement has total N-m and uniquely determines the selected cycle-type multiset. Hence |Lambda(F,m)| <= p(N-m). Proof: any A with F(A)=A and F|A bijective consists entirely of complete cycles of F, since every x in A lies on a finite permutation orbit under F|A; the added singleton parts represent the nonperiodic states. The selected parts have total m, so their complement has total N-m. Multiset subtraction from the fixed padded partition is injective. This is the complete combinatorial argument; the restriction m>N/2 is unnecessary for this lemma.

The unrolling construction is correct: wiring each update circuit F_t's state outputs to F_{t+1}'s state inputs, feeding x_t to its update, hard-wiring the initial state, and connecting the final state to readout D yields a valid fan-in-2 Boolean circuit computing L. Induction on t confirms the intermediate wires match the streaming machine's state after each prefix. The composed circuit uses exactly the gates from F_1,...,F_N and D with no additional gates needed for state wiring or hard-wiring constants. Since L has minimum fan-in-2 circuit complexity h, the composed circuit's gate count (bounded above by sum_t size(F_t)+size(D)) must be at least h, so the streaming realization's total gate cost is >= h. This holds for every state-space size because the gate count of the unrolled circuit is independent of the state width. No counterexample or argument gap found.

statement: Residual-state characterization. Let L be a language over a finite alphabet with finitely many distinct suffix residuals L_u = {v : uv ∈ L}. The minimum number of states in a deterministic recognizer that reads one symbol per transition and decides L at end of input equals the number of distinct residuals.
proof: If two prefixes reach the same state, every suffix has the same acceptance outcome after either prefix, so their residuals are equal. Thus distinct residuals require distinct states. Conversely, take the residuals as states, start at L_ε, transition from L_u on symbol a to L_{ua}, and accept L_u exactly when ε ∈ L_u. This transition is well-defined: equality L_u = L_{u'} implies, for every suffix v, av ∈ L_u iff av ∈ L_{u'}, hence v ∈ L_{ua} iff v ∈ L_{u'a}; therefore L_{ua} = L_{u'a}. Induction on input length proves that the resulting automaton accepts exactly L.
scope: Finite residual set; deterministic exact one-pass recognition with an end-of-input decision. This is a state-count result only, not a transition-gate lower bound or P-vs-NP result.

evidence: The padded omitted-cycle bound is correct. Let C be the multiset of cycle lengths of F, r the number of non-periodic states. Form lambda by adjoining r formal parts of size 1 to C. Every admissible A of size m with F(A)=A and F|A bijective consists of whole cycles of F (since F|A is a permutation). Its cycle-type multiset sigma(A) is a submultiset of lambda with total m. The complement in lambda has total N-m and uniquely determines sigma(A). Distinct sigma(A) give distinct complements, so |Lambda(F,m)| <= number of partitions of N-m = p(N-m). The padding parts are formal and not claimed to be cycles of F, so the construction is valid. No counterexample found; the argument is sound.

proved_step: statement: LEMMA (fan-in k ancestor bound). Let C be a Boolean circuit with one output, gates of fan-in at most k for an integer k>=2, and suppose the output depends on N>=2 distinct primary inputs. Then C has at least (N-1)/(k-1) gates. Proof: Retain only the g' gates in the output's ancestor cone. Form the undirected graph with these gates and the N relevant input vertices, joining a gate to every gate or relevant input supplying one of its wires. The graph is connected: every retained gate reaches the output, and every relevant input reaches a retained gate. It has at most k g' edges, since each gate has at most k incoming wires and identifying repeated wires only decreases the edge count. A connected graph on N+g' vertices has at least N+g'-1 edges. Thus N+g'-1<=kg', so g'>=(N-1)/(k-1), and the full circuit has at least that many gates. This applies also to an unrolled deterministic streaming computation whenever its final output depends on all N streamed inputs; its total update-plus-readout gate cost is at least (N-1)/(k-1). Scope: fan-in at most k, one output, N relevant primary inputs; the consequence is linear and gives no superlinear streaming cost bound.

statement: LEMMA (finite-basis circuit-pair count). Fix a finite fan-in-two gate basis of size B, and integers S>=1 and G>=0. The number of ordered pairs (F,H) of acyclic Boolean circuits, each with S input bits and S designated output bits, whose total number of gates is at most G, is at most (G+1)^2 B^G (S+G+2)^(2G+2S). Proof: For exactly g and h gates with g+h<=G, topologically order gates. Each gate has at most B choices of type and at most (S+G+2)^2 choices for its two predecessor signals (primary inputs, constants, or earlier gates); each of the 2S designated output wires has at most S+G+2 choices. Thus for fixed g,h the number is at most B^(g+h)(S+G+2)^(2(g+h)+2S), bounded by B^G(S+G+2)^(2G+2S). There are at most (G+1)^2 choices of (g,h); summing proves the bound. Invalid encodings and multiple topological encodings only increase the count.
scope: All S>=1, G>=0, and any fixed finite basis of B fan-in-two gate types; ordered circuit pairs with S input bits and S designated output wires each, counting gate count in aggregate. Syntactic counting only, not a state-recoding lower bound.

evidence: The stated circuit-count hypothesis omits the cost of choosing the 2S designated output wires. This makes the asymptotic conclusion unsupported for the actual C_G when G is very small (in particular G=0), since even zero-gate circuits have output-wire choices. Repair: encoding each pair with g+h≤G gates by gate types, predecessor wires, and 2S outputs gives C_G≤(G+1)^2 B^G(S+G+2)^(2G+2S), hence log C_G=O_B((G+S)log(G+S+2)). For S=ceil(log₂N) and G=o(√N/log N), this corrected logarithm is still o(√N), so the fixed-density counting comparison can be re-proved under the corrected bound. The corrected circuit-count estimate is S0485 and remains CLAIMED; this review refutes the stated hypothesis as written, not the fixed-density direction.

statement: REPAIR LEMMA (uniform encoding count with designated outputs). Fix a finite fan-in-two basis of size B>=1, S>=1 primary inputs per circuit, and G>=0 total gates across an ordered pair of circuits, each with one designated output. The number of syntactic ordered circuit pairs with at most G gates total is at most (G+1)^2 B^G(S+G+2)^(2G+2). Proof: choose gate counts g,h with g+h<=G (at most (G+1)^2 choices). In a fixed topological order, each of g+h gates has a type and two predecessor indices among at most S+G+1 signals, giving at most B^G(S+G+1)^(2G) encodings. Each circuit's designated output is one of at most S+G signals, so the pair contributes at most (S+G)^2 choices. Multiplying and enlarging bases yields the stated bound. This explicitly includes the output-wire choices missing from the earlier count. The bound is syntactic and may overcount functionally equivalent circuits.
scope: Finite fan-in-two basis, S>=1 inputs per circuit, ordered pair, at most G total gates, one designated output per circuit.

statement: REPAIRED EXISTENCE LEMMA (hard pair of maps uniformly over stationary encodings). Fix a finite fan-in-two gate basis of size B>=1. For all sufficiently large m, with S=ceil(log2 m), there exist maps delta_0,delta_1:[m]->[m] and a constant epsilon>0 such that, for every injection psi:[m]->{0,1}^S, any pair of circuits whose outputs on the encoded states realize psi delta_0 psi^{-1} and psi delta_1 psi^{-1} has total gate count greater than epsilon m. Proof: For a fixed encoding and a circuit pair, restricting both circuits to the m encoded states determines at most one pair of maps [m]->[m] (pairs whose outputs fail to decode to valid codes realize no such map pair). By S0487, the number of syntactic circuit pairs of total size at most G is at most (G+1)^2 B^G(S+G+2)^(2G+2). Thus at most m! (G+1)^2 B^G(S+G+2)^(2G+2) encoding/map-pair incidences are represented. There are m^(2m) map pairs. Choose G=floor(epsilon m), for a sufficiently small fixed epsilon, for example any epsilon<1/8. The base-2 logarithm of the incidence bound is at most log2(m!)+2log2(G+1)+G log2(B)+(2G+2)log2(S+G+2) = (1+2epsilon+o(1))m log2(m), which is not small enough for this choice of incidence comparison. Therefore this direct counting argument does NOT prove the stated conclusion; the claimed lemma is withdrawn. Corrected usable consequence: if instead the encoding family has size at most m! and the map-pair family has size m^(2m), this same count only yields a contradiction when the circuit-pair count is less than m^m, which the displayed bound does not ensure for G=epsilon*m. No recoding lower bound is established by this count.
scope: Finite set [m], injective stationary encodings into S=ceil(log2 m) bits, fixed finite fan-in-two basis; this records the exact failure of the attempted counting extension, not a lower bound.

statement: LEMMA (uniform count with designated outputs). Fix B>=1, S>=1 and G>=0. The number of syntactic ordered pairs of fan-in-two circuits over a fixed basis of size B, each with S inputs and one designated output, using at most G gates total, is at most (G+1)^2 B^G(S+G+2)^(2G+2). Proof: Choose gate counts g,h with g+h<=G; there are at most (G+1)^2 choices. In a fixed topological order, encode each gate by its type and its two predecessor signals, each selected from at most S+G+1 available signals. This gives at most B^G(S+G+1)^(2G) encodings. Encode the two designated outputs by at most (S+G)^2 further choices. Since S+G+1 and S+G are at most S+G+2, the product is at most the displayed bound for each count pair, and summing over count pairs proves the claim.
scope: Syntactic circuit count; fixed finite basis, ordered pair, at most G total gates, one designated output per circuit.

evidence: The claimed inference from m^{2m} <= m! 2^{c(G+S)log2(G+S)} to a contradiction for G=floor(epsilon m) is invalid for an arbitrary fixed c: the displayed upper bound on log2(m!) is fine, but choosing epsilon so that c*epsilon < 1/2 still does not justify c*(G+S)log2(G+S) <= (1/2)m log2 m uniformly for all sufficiently large m unless epsilon is chosen with the appropriate constant factor; more decisively, even if that bound holds, the RHS logarithm is at most (3/2)m log2 m, while the premise only gives 2m log2 m <= log2(m!)+..., which is a necessary inequality for coverage. Its failure does prove noncoverage. The step is not refuted by that reasoning. Need exact counterexample or gap.

statement: LEMMA (all-injection counting repair). Fix a complete fan-in-2 Boolean basis. Suppose the number of ordered pairs of S-input, S-output circuits with at most G total gates is at most 2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)} for a basis-dependent constant c. For all sufficiently large m, with S=ceil(log_2 m), there are two maps on an m-element set such that for every injection into {0,1}^S, circuits implementing both maps on the encoded states require more than epsilon*m gates total, for some fixed epsilon>0. Proof: q=2^S and the number of injections is (q)_m, at most q^m<(2m)^m. For each injection and circuit pair, restricting to encoded inputs and decoding outputs determines at most one pair of maps, so at most (q)_m*2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)} map pairs are representable with total cost at most G under some injection. There are m^{2m} ordered map pairs. Set G=floor(epsilon*m). For sufficiently small fixed epsilon and sufficiently large m, m log_2(2m)+c(G+S)log_2(G+S)<2m log_2(m), since the first term is m log_2(m)+O(m), and the coefficient of m log_2(m) in the second term can be made less than one by choosing epsilon small. Thus fewer than m^{2m} map pairs are represented; some pair has no such encoding and circuit pair. This is an existence result, not an explicit hard pair or P-vs-NP consequence. Barrier diagnostic: no P-vs-NP progress claimed; the counting method is nonconstructive, no natural property or learner is obtained, and relativizing/algebrizing/localizing status is not used to infer a target lower bound. The perfect-matching control does not apply as a transferable restricted-model bound to a function in P; no natural-measure lower bound is claimed.
scope: All sufficiently large m under the stated fan-in-2 circuit-counting hypothesis; all stationary injective encodings into S=ceil(log_2 m) bits; arbitrary ordered pairs of total maps, evaluated only on encoded states.

evidence: The argument is sound: 1) The padded omitted-cycle bound (S0471, survived review) gives |Λ(F,m)| ≤ p(N−m). 2) Circuit count C_G = 2^{O(G log(G+S))} with S=Θ(log N). 3) If G = o(√N/log N), then log C_G = o(√N). 4) Hardy-Ramanujan gives log p(m) − log p(N−m) ≥ c_ε√N + o(√N) for m ≥ (1/2+ε)N. 5) Eventually C_G p(N−m) < p(m), so some partition of m is missed. statement: Conditional counting lemma: Fix c>0 and m>=2, let S=ceil(log_2 m), and suppose the number of ordered pairs of fan-in-2 Boolean circuits with S input bits and S output bits and total size at most G is at most 2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)}. For all sufficiently large m there exist maps delta_0,delta_1:[m]->[m] such that for every injection psi:[m]->{0,1}^S, any circuit pair implementing both conjugated maps on psi([m]) has total size greater than floor(epsilon m), for epsilon=1/(4c). Proof: There are m^{2m} ordered pairs of maps. There are (2^S)_m <= 2^{Sm} injections. For any fixed injection and circuit pair, its outputs on the m encoded states determine at most one pair of maps on [m]. Hence the number of map pairs representable with total circuit size <=G under some injection is at most 2^{Sm+c(G+S)log_2(G+S)}. For G=floor(epsilon m), S=O(log m), the base-2 logarithm of this bound divided by m log_2 m tends to 1+c epsilon=5/4, whereas log_2(m^{2m})/(m log_2 m)=2. Thus for all sufficiently large m the representable count is strictly less than m^{2m}, proving existence of a pair outside it. This is non-explicit and conditional on the circuit-pair counting hypothesis.
scope: Conditional asymptotic existence statement under the explicitly stated circuit-pair counting bound; stationary injective encodings with exactly S=ceil(log_2 m) bits. No explicit hard pair or P-vs-NP consequence.

statement: LEMMA (exact streamed-parity cost). For every N>=2, among deterministic one-pass realizations of parity on x_1,...,x_N with fixed initial state and fan-in-at-most-two Boolean update and readout circuits, the minimum of sum_t size(F_t)+size(D) is exactly N-1. Lower bound: unroll the updates and readout into a fan-in-at-most-two circuit C with g no greater than that sum. In the output ancestor cone let g' be its number of gates and e the number of gate-to-gate input wires, counted with multiplicity. The cone’s gate graph is connected, so e>=g'-1. There are at most 2g'-e<=g'+1 slots for primary-input wires. Each of the N variables must occur in such a slot because parity depends on every variable. Thus N<=g'+1<=g+1, giving total cost >=N-1. Upper bound: use a one-bit state. The first update copies x_1 into the state using wiring and no gates; for each t=2,...,N update the state to state XOR x_t using one XOR gate; the readout copies the final state using wiring and no gates. This computes parity and has total gate cost N-1.
scope: Exact minimum total gate cost for deterministic one-pass parity on N>=2 streamed Boolean inputs, fixed initial state, fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuits, and gate count excluding wires.

statement: For a fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit with g gates and r designated outputs, if those outputs collectively depend on N distinct primary inputs, then N <= g+2r. Proof: In the union of their ancestor cones, let c be the number of connected components of the gate wiring graph; each component contains an output ancestor, so c <= r. Each component with h gates has at least h-1 gate-to-gate input slots occupied, since its gate graph is connected. Thus at most 2g-(g-c)=g+c gate-input slots can carry primary inputs. At most r more distinct inputs can be designated directly as outputs. Therefore N <= g+c+r <= g+2r.
scope: Finite fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuits; counts distinct primary inputs on which at least one of r designated outputs depends.
proof: Complete proof given in statement.

statement: For any fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit with g gates and designated output bits f_1,...,f_r, let d_j be the number of distinct primary input variables on which f_j essentially depends. Then g >= max_j(d_j-1). Consequently, for any fixed state encoding and any transition circuit computing the encoded transition on valid states, its gate count is at least max_j(d_j-1), where d_j is computed for the circuit's actual Boolean extension to all bit strings.
scope: Finite Boolean circuits; the consequence applies to any chosen circuit extension of a transition map from valid encoded states.
proof: Fix j and restrict to the ancestor cone of output f_j, with h gates. The gate-wiring graph is connected, so at least h-1 gate-input slots are occupied by gate outputs. At most 2h-(h-1)=h+1 slots remain for primary inputs. Every essential primary input of f_j must occur in one of these slots, hence d_j<=h+1 and h>=d_j-1. Since h<=g, g>=d_j-1 for every j; taking the maximum proves the claim.

statement: Counting lemma for permutation transitions. Let Q be an m-element state set, m>=2, encoded injectively by ψ:Q→{0,1}^S, where S=ceil(log2 m). Use fan-in-two Boolean circuits with arbitrary two-input Boolean gates, constants, and S designated output bits. If the transition family contains every permutation δ:Q→Q, then for every encoding ψ some δ has no circuit computing ψ∘δ∘ψ^{-1} on ψ(Q) with fewer than c m gates, for an absolute constant c>0 and all sufficiently large m. Proof: There are m! distinct encoded transition maps on ψ(Q), since conjugation by ψ is injective on permutations. The number of circuits with at most g gates and S outputs is at most (g+1)(16(S+g)^2)^g(S+g)^S: choose each gate’s truth table and its two incoming wires, then choose each output wire. For g=cm, its base-two logarithm is at most O(cm log m)+O(S log m). Since log2(m!)=m log2 m-O(m), choose a sufficiently small absolute c; for all sufficiently large m the circuit count is less than m!. Thus at least one encoded permutation map is not computed by any circuit of at most cm gates. The argument is independent of ψ, so it holds for every stationary encoding.
scope: Transition family contains all permutations of Q; stationary injective encodings into S=ceil(log2 m) bits; arbitrary fan-in-two Boolean gates; circuit correctness required only on valid encoded states.
proof: Complete counting proof is included in the statement.

LEMMA (multi-output incidence bound). Let C be a fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit with g gates, r designated output wires, and N distinct primary inputs that are relevant to at least one designated output. Then g >= N-r. Proof: Delete every gate and input irrelevant to all designated outputs, and let g' be the number of remaining gates. Form an undirected graph on the remaining gates and relevant inputs, joining each gate to the gate or input supplying each incoming wire. Every component contains a designated output gate or an input that is itself a designated output; hence the number c of components is at most r. The graph has at most 2g' edges, since each edge is charged to an incoming slot of a gate. A graph on N+g' vertices with c components has at least N+g'-c edges. Thus N+g'-c <= 2g', so g' >= N-c >= N-r, and g >= g'. The -r term accounts for direct input-to-output wires. This sharpens multi-output incidence accounting but does not imply a superlinear state-recoding cost.

LEMMA (multi-output incidence bound, explicit output convention). Let C be a finite acyclic Boolean circuit with fan-in at most two, g gates, and r designated output wires. Let N be the number of distinct primary input variables on which at least one designated output function depends. Then g >= N-r. Proof: Delete every gate and primary input that is irrelevant to all designated outputs, and let g'<=g be the remaining gate count. Form an undirected graph whose vertices are the g' gates and the N relevant primary inputs. Join a gate to each gate or primary input supplying one of its input slots; constants contribute no vertex, and repeated connections may be represented by one edge. Every remaining gate is an ancestor of a designated output, and every relevant input has a path to a gate ancestor of a designated output unless that output is directly the input. Thus each connected component contains a driver of at least one designated output wire. This includes direct input outputs; duplicate output wires may have the same driver, so the number c of components is at most r. The graph has at least N+g'-c edges. It has at most 2g' edges, since each edge is charged to an incoming slot of a gate. Hence N+g'-c<=2g', so g'>=N-c>=N-r, and g>=N-r. This statement counts output wires separately and allows direct and duplicate outputs. It is only a linear incidence bound.
