proved_step: statement: Corrected cycle-inventory lemma: Let X be finite, F:X→X, and let a_i be the number of directed cycles of length i. For every integer m≥0, the number of subsets A⊆X of size m such that F|A:A→A is bijective equals [z^m] ∏_{i≥1}(1+z^i)^{a_i}. Proof: If F|A is bijective, each forward orbit from a∈A remains in A and, by finiteness, reaches a cycle. A nonempty tail entering that cycle would give its entry vertex two distinct predecessors in A, contradicting injectivity of F|A. Hence every element of A is periodic. Periodic points partition into disjoint cycles, and if A contains one point of a cycle, forward closure forces it to contain the entire cycle. Conversely, any union of complete cycles is mapped bijectively to itself. For each i, choosing b_i of the a_i distinct length-i cycles contributes binom(a_i,b_i) subsets of size i b_i. Summing over all b_i with Σ_i i b_i=m gives the coefficient of ∏_i Σ_{b=0}^{a_i} binom(a_i,b)z^{ib}=∏_i(1+z^i)^{a_i}.

statement: Subset multiplicity lemma. Let X be finite, F:X→X, and let a_i denote the number of i-cycles of F. For each m≥0, the number of m-element subsets A⊆X for which F|A is bijective equals [z^m]∏_{i≥1}(1+z^i)^{a_i}. Moreover, for any feasible cycle type specified by integers b_i with 0≤b_i≤a_i and Σ_i i b_i=m, exactly ∏_i binom(a_i,b_i) such subsets realize that type. Proof: If F|A is bijective, then F(A)=A and injectivity rules out any nonperiodic tail in A entering a cycle, since the cycle-entry vertex would have both its cycle predecessor and its tail predecessor in A. Thus A is a union of full cycles. Conversely, every union of full cycles is invariant and F restricts to a bijection. To realize type (b_i), independently choose b_i of the a_i distinct i-cycles, giving ∏_i binom(a_i,b_i) subsets; summing by total cardinality yields the displayed generating function.

proved_step: statement: Subset-counting repair lemma. For a finite set X, a self-map F:X→X, and a_i the number of directed cycles of length i in F, the number of m-element subsets A⊆X for which F|A is bijective is [z^m]∏_{i≥1}(1+z^i)^{a_i}. More precisely, a feasible type (b_i), where 0≤b_i≤a_i and Σ_i i b_i=m, is realized by exactly ∏_i binom(a_i,b_i) such subsets. Proof: If F|A is bijective, then F(A)=A and F|A is injective. If x∈A were not periodic, its forward orbit would first enter a cycle at some y∈A; y then has both its cycle predecessor and the preceding tail vertex as distinct preimages in A, contradicting injectivity. So every element of A lies on a full cycle, and A is a union of full cycles. Conversely any union of full cycles is F-invariant and F restricts to a bijection. A type (b_i) is obtained by choosing b_i of the a_i distinct i-cycles independently for every i, giving ∏_i binom(a_i,b_i) subsets. Summing these multiplicities over feasible types gives [z^m]∏_i Σ_{b=0}^{a_i} binom(a_i,b)z^{ib}=[z^m]∏_i(1+z^i)^{a_i}. This separates the unweighted distinct-type count in S0570 from the subset count.

For every integer m≥2 and every permutation δ on an m-element set Q consisting of one cycle, there is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log₂m), such that ψδψ⁻¹ extends to a total Boolean map on S bits computed by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. statement: HAMMING-DISPLACEMENT EXTENSION LEMMA. Let Q be an m-element set, m≥2, S=ceil(log₂m), and ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective. For any map δ:Q→Q, let T={q:δ(q)≠q} and h_q be the Hamming distance between ψ(q) and ψ(δ(q)). There is a total Boolean map F:{0,1}^S→{0,1}^S agreeing with ψ∘δ∘ψ⁻¹ on ψ(Q), computable by O(S+∑_{q∈T}h_q) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: For each q∈T construct the indicator e_q(x)=1 iff x=ψ(q), as the conjunction of the S literals matching ψ(q); this costs O(S+|T|S) gates including shared input negations. For each coordinate j define D_j={q∈T:ψ(q)_j≠ψ(δ(q))_j} and F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q∈D_j} e_q(x)), with the empty OR equal to zero. Implement OR with fan-in-two AND/NOT gates by De Morgan, and XOR using a constant number of such gates per term. The indicator costs are not yet within the claimed bound, so instead exploit the fact that each e_q is only needed for its h_q changed coordinates: compute a separate equality conjunction for each pair (q,j) with q∈D_j, at O(S) gates apiece, and share it across the output formula for that coordinate only. This gives O(S∑h_q) gates, not the claimed additive bound. Thus the claimed O(S+∑h_q) bound does not follow from this construction; the valid bound is O(S+S∑h_q), and a sharper bound requires a new construction.

COMMON-POWER-OF-TWO-CYCLE LEMMA. Let m=t·2^k, where t≥1 and k≥0, and let F be a permutation on an m-element set whose cycles all have length 2^k. With S=ceil(log₂m), there is an injection ψ into {0,1}^S such that ψFψ⁻¹ extends to a Boolean map on {0,1}^S computed by O(log m) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Index each state by (i,j), with 0≤i<t and 0≤j<2^k, so F(i,j)=(i,j+1 mod 2^k). Encode (i,j) by the concatenation of the ceil(log₂t)-bit binary encoding of i and the k-bit encoding of j; the total width is ceil(log₂t)+k=ceil(log₂(t·2^k))=S. The output high field copies i. The low field computes j+1 modulo 2^k, using an incrementer with O(k) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates; for k=0 the map is the identity. This defines the map on all S-bit strings, including unused high-field encodings, and agrees with F on every encoded state. Since k≤log₂m, its size is O(log m). Diagnostic: relativizing/natural/algebrizing/localizing status is not assessed as a P≠NP claim; no P≠NP progress or transfer is asserted.

statement: Let m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and delta:Q->Q change exactly t states. Then psi delta psi^{-1} extends to a total Boolean map computed by O(S(1+t)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: For each changed q form e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] as the AND of its S matching literals, sharing input negations; this costs O(St). For each bit j, let D_j be the changed states where psi(q)_j differs from psi(delta(q))_j, and set F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x). OR and XOR have constant-size fan-in-two AND/NOT implementations per operation, so all outputs cost O(S+sum_j |D_j|)=O(S+St). At an encoded unchanged state all indicators vanish. At an encoded changed state injectivity makes exactly its indicator active, toggling precisely the destination's differing bits. Thus F agrees with the encoded transition on psi(Q); its formula defines values on unused codes too. For m=1, S=0 and the unique transition has a zero-gate extension.

evidence: The proposed construction sends the last state of cycle i to the first state of cycle i+1 when it says to increment the cycle index at a wrap. By definition of F, that state must map to the first state of the same cycle i. The encoding therefore fails to represent F for any instance with at least two cycles; the claimed bound is not proved by this construction.

proved_step: UNEQUAL-CYCLE INTERVAL-ENCODING LEMMA. Let m>=2, Q be an m-element set, and delta a permutation of Q with r cycles. Put S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computed by O(rS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: List the cycles in any order, with lengths ell_1,...,ell_r, and label their states consecutively 0,...,m-1, respecting cyclic order within each cycle. Encode each state by its S-bit binary label. A shared S-bit incrementer computes x+1 modulo 2^S using O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, since carry prefixes are built successively and XOR has constant-size AND/NOT implementation. For each cycle interval [a_i,b_i], build the equality indicator e_i(x)=[x=b_i], using O(S) gates. Starting from the incrementer output, for each i and each output bit j override that bit at e_i=1 with bit j of a_i; each override costs O(1), so all endpoint corrections cost O(rS). The resulting total map agrees with the cycle successor at every encoded label: non-endpoints increment to the next label in their interval, while b_i maps to a_i. It is defined on unused labels and other bit strings by the same circuit, and psi is injective because labels are distinct. Thus the total cost is O(S+rS)=O(rS).

lemma: Explicit single-cycle increment-and-mask construction: for every m>=2 with S=ceil(log2 m), there is an injective encoding of an m-cycle into {0,1}^S whose encoded transition extends to a total S-bit map computed by at most 8S+2 fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: encode cycle states 0,...,m-1 by their S-bit binary expansions, least significant bit first. For an arbitrary input x, compute increment bits y_0=NOT x_0 and y_j=x_j XOR c_j for j>=1, where c_1=x_0 and c_{j+1}=c_j AND x_j. The carries use at most S-1 gates, y_0 uses one NOT, and each XOR can be implemented in at most five AND/NOT gates using XOR=(a OR b) AND NOT(a AND b), with OR implemented by De Morgan. Let e(x) be the indicator that x is the code for m-1. Its literal conjunction costs at most S-1 AND gates and at most S input negations. Define F_j(x)=y_j AND NOT e(x), computing NOT e once and using S final AND gates. The total is bounded by (S-1)+1+5(S-1)+(S-1)+S+1+S <= 8S+2. For codes 0,...,m-2, e=0 and F increments; for m-1, e=1 and F=0. Hence the required cycle transition is correct. The same formula defines a total map on all unused encodings.

statement: For every m>=2, with S=ceil(log2 m), an m-cycle has an injective encoding into {0,1}^S whose transition extends to a total S-bit map computed by at most 9S fan-in-two AND/NOT gates; constants and input wires are free.
proof: Number the cycle states 0,...,m-1 and encode each by its S-bit binary expansion, least significant bit first. For any input x, compute increment bits y_0=NOT x_0 and y_j=x_j XOR c_j for j>=1, where c_1=x_0 and c_{j+1}=c_j AND x_j. The carries use at most S-1 gates, y_0 uses one NOT, and each XOR uses at most five AND/NOT gates via XOR=(a OR b) AND NOT(a AND b), with OR implemented by De Morgan. Let e(x) test whether x encodes m-1: its literal negations cost at most S gates and its conjunction at most S-1 AND gates. Compute NOT e once, then output F_j=y_j AND NOT e using S gates. The total is at most (S-1)+1+5(S-1)+S+(S-1)+1+S=9S-5<=9S. On codes below m-1, F increments; on m-1, F outputs zero, so it implements the cycle. The same circuit defines F on unused encodings.

statement: Involution encoding lemma. Let m>=2, Q be an m-element set, and delta:Q->Q satisfy delta(delta(q))=q for every q. Put S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi∘delta∘psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map on {0,1}^S computable by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: The orbits of delta are t two-element orbits and f fixed points, where 2t+f=m. Enumerate the pairs and encode their elements by 2r and 2r+1 for r=0,...,t-1; encode the fixed points by 2t,...,m-1. These are distinct integers below m and therefore fit in S bits. On every S-bit string x define F(x) to toggle its least significant bit if x<2t, and otherwise fix x. For each encoded pair, F interchanges its two codes; for each encoded fixed point, F fixes its code. Thus F agrees with the encoded transition on psi(Q). The comparison x<2t has an O(S)-gate fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit: lexicographically compare the S-bit strings from most significant to least significant, maintaining equality and less-than flags with O(1) gates per bit. The conditional toggle also uses O(S) gates (compute the comparison once and XOR its result into the low bit). Hence F has O(S) gates. This proves the claim.
evidence: Independent finite verification cm-456b8f9663494506 enumerated all 1,115 involutions for 1<=m<=8 and checked 8,845 bit strings, with no failures. This is a finite implementation check; the proof above is general. This session cannot assign a closure because the current proof-state read must identify a pre-existing open-obligation id first.

lemma: For m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), any injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S and any map delta:Q->Q, the encoded transition psi delta psi^{-1} extends to a total S-bit Boolean map with O(mS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: for each q form the minterm e_q for psi(q), using O(S) gates; for each output coordinate j OR the e_q whose image psi(delta(q)) has bit j equal to 1. The outputs agree on all encoded states, and values on unused codes are unrestricted. Total cost O(mS).
evidence: Direct minterm synthesis and coordinatewise disjunction; complete proof included. This is a general fallback upper bound, not a lower bound or P-vs-NP result.

statement: For every m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), finite m-element Q, injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S, and transition delta:Q->Q, the partial encoded map psi∘delta∘psi^{-1} extends to a total Boolean map on S bits computed by O(mS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates.
proof: For each q in Q let e_q(x) be the conjunction of the S literals specifying psi(q). This costs O(S) gates per q, hence O(mS) total. For coordinate j define F_j(x)=OR_{q: bit_j(psi(delta(q)))=1} e_q(x), with empty OR equal to 0. Each OR is implementable using fan-in-two AND/NOT gates with linear cost in its number of terms, so all output ORs cost O(mS). At x=psi(q0), injectivity implies e_q(x)=1 exactly when q=q0; hence F_j(psi(q0))=bit_j(psi(delta(q0))) for every j. The formulas define values on unused codes, which are unrestricted. Thus F extends the encoded transition with O(mS) gates.

statement: For all integers t>=1 and k>=0, if Q is partitioned into t directed cycles each of length 2^k, there is an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^{ceil(log2 |Q|)} under which the cycle transition is computed on encoded states by an AND/NOT fan-in-two circuit with O(k) gates, independent of t. Encode state (i,j) as binary(i)||binary_k(j), preserve i as output wires, and update j by incrementing modulo 2^k.
proof: Identify each state with (i,j), 0<=i<t and 0<=j<2^k, and encode it as binary(i)||binary_k(j). The width is ceil(log2 t)+k=ceil(log2(t*2^k)). Set carry c_0=1 and c_{r+1}=c_r AND j_r. Output phase bit r as j_r XOR c_r; XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. Shared carries yield O(k) gates total; index bits pass through as wires. For k=0 the transition is identity. This computes the designated transition on every encoded state; unused codes may take arbitrary outputs.

proved_step: statement: Universal truth-table synthesis bound for finite transitions. For every m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), every m-element set Q, every map delta:Q->Q, and every injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S, the partial conjugate psi delta psi^{-1} extends to a total map F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S computed by at most m(S-1)+S(m-1)+S fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (constants and input wires free). Proof: For each q in Q, let e_q(x) be the conjunction of the S literals specifying psi(q); compute all m indicators using at most m(S-1) gates, with input negations shared. For each output coordinate j define F_j(x)=OR_{q: bit_j(psi(delta(q)))=1} e_q(x), using at most m-1 binary OR gates, each expressible with AND/NOT and shared input negations. On x=psi(q0), injectivity gives e_q0=1 and e_q=0 for q!=q0, so F_j(x)=bit_j(psi(delta(q0))) for every j. The same formulas define F on unused strings, hence a total extension. The gate count is at most m(S-1)+S(m-1), plus at most S shared negations, and is O(m log m). The result holds for every fixed encoding, so it gives a universal ceiling for max_delta min_psi, but does not prove the target sqrt(m)-scale bounds.

statement: For every m>=2 and a_0,a_1 in Z_m, let Q=Z_m and delta_b(x)=x+a_b mod m for b in {0,1}. With S=ceil(log_2 m), there is a common injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that each partial map psi delta_b psi^{-1} extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computed by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (constants and wires free). Proof: encode x by its S-bit binary expansion. For a fixed a in [0,m-1], compute u=x+a modulo 2^S using the usual ripple-carry recurrence; each bit's carry is a Boolean function of the prior carry and the current input bit, so each stage uses O(1) fan-in-two gates and all stages use O(S). Compare u with the constant m using a ripple comparator, O(S) gates. If u>=m, subtract m using a ripple subtractor, O(S) gates; otherwise keep u. Since x<m and a<m, x+a<2m, so the result after this single conditional subtraction is exactly (x+a) mod m. This defines a total map on all S-bit inputs; on encoded states it agrees with delta. Apply the construction separately to a_0 and a_1 under the same encoding. Thus each transition has O(S) gates and the encoding is common.
proof: As stated in the full statement field; the arithmetic is correct because 0<=x,a<m implies 0<=x+a<2m, so at most one subtraction of m is required after addition. Ripple addition, comparison with a fixed constant, and conditional fixed-constant subtraction each have O(S)-gate fan-in-two implementations.

statement: Sparse baseline-correction lemma: Let Q be an m-element set, S>=1, psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective, and beta,delta:Q->Q differ on t states. If a total S-bit fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit F0 of B gates satisfies F0(psi(q))=psi(beta(q)) for every q, then there is a total S-bit fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit F of at most B+O((t+1)S) gates satisfying F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for every q. Proof: For each exceptional q, form the S-literal indicator e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)], using O(tS) gates total. For output coordinate j, let D_j be exceptional q where psi(delta(q))_j differs from psi(beta(q))_j. Define F_j=F0_j XOR OR_{q in D_j} e_q. Fan-in-two AND/NOT circuits implement each OR and XOR with O(1) gates per term, so all corrections cost O(sum_j |D_j|+S)=O(tS+S). On each encoded q, injectivity makes only e_q true; therefore the output toggles exactly the coordinates where baseline differs from target. On unchanged states all indicators vanish. Thus F agrees with psi composed with delta composed with psi inverse on psi(Q); its values off psi(Q) are supplied by the same total formula.

statement: For every integer m>=2, every epsilon in {-1,1}, and every a in Z_m, the affine transition delta(x)=epsilon*x+a mod m on Q=Z_m has an O(log m)-gate fan-in-two AND/NOT implementation under the common binary encoding psi(x)=x in {0,1}^S, S=ceil(log_2 m), with arbitrary values permitted on unused encodings.
proof: For an S-bit input x, compute u=x+a mod 2^S when epsilon=1; when epsilon=-1, compute u=a-x mod 2^S. Ripple addition or subtraction uses O(S) fan-in-two gates. Compare u with m and conditionally subtract m if u>=m. For epsilon=1 and 0<=x,a<m, x+a<2m, so at most one subtraction yields (x+a) mod m. For epsilon=-1, choose the representative a-x mod 2^S; when x>a this is 2^S-(x-a), which may exceed m, so one subtraction is not sufficient to reduce modulo m. Instead compute the signed difference with a borrow bit, then select a-x if x<=a or m-(x-a) if x>a; comparison, subtraction, and selection each take O(S) gates. This yields the required residue on every encoded x. The circuit is total on all S-bit inputs, and its unused-code behavior is unrestricted.

statement: For every integer m>=2, every epsilon in {-1,1}, and every a in Z_m, the affine map delta(x)=epsilon*x+a mod m on Z_m has a total extension under the binary encoding into S=ceil(log2 m) bits computable by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (constants and wires free).
proof: Encode each state x in {0,...,m-1} by its S-bit binary expansion. If epsilon=1, compute the full (S+1)-bit sum z=x+a, retaining the carry. Since x,a<m, z<2m, so output z-m if z>=m and z otherwise. Ripple addition, comparison to the fixed constant m, conditional subtraction, and selection each use O(S) fan-in-two gates. If epsilon=-1, compare x with a; output a-x when x<=a and m-(x-a) when x>a. Fixed-width comparison/subtraction and selection each use O(S) gates. Both formulas return the desired residue on every valid encoded state; the circuits define a total map on all S-bit strings, with arbitrary behavior permitted on unused codes.

statement: Multi-cycle interval encoding lemma. Let Q be an m-element set, m>=2, and let δ be a permutation of Q with c disjoint cycles. Set S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^S and a total S-bit Boolean map F agreeing with ψ∘δ∘ψ^{-1} on ψ(Q), computed by O((c+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: Order the cycles arbitrarily, with lengths ℓ_1,...,ℓ_c, and identify their states in successor order with consecutive integers in disjoint intervals [a_i,a_i+ℓ_i−1] partitioning {0,...,m−1}. Encode each state by its S-bit binary integer. Let Inc(x) be ordinary S-bit increment modulo 2^S, computed with O(S) gates by shared prefix carries. For each cycle i form the equality indicator e_i(x)=[x=a_i+ℓ_i−1], costing O(S) gates each with shared input negations. On every non-endpoint encoded state, Inc is its successor code. At endpoint i, the desired output is a_i; obtain it by toggling exactly the coordinates where Inc(a_i+ℓ_i−1) differs from a_i, conditioned on e_i. Thus F_j(x)=Inc_j(x) XOR OR_{i: Inc_j(a_i+ℓ_i−1)≠(a_i)_j} e_i(x). The indicators are mutually exclusive since endpoints are distinct. Increment costs O(S), all equality tests O(cS), and output corrections O(cS); hence total O((c+1)S). This defines F on every bit string and is correct on every encoded state. The construction handles singleton cycles as well.

gap: Extends the recorded O(log m) construction for slopes +/-1 to every fixed multiplier u modulo m, with an O(log^2 m) circuit construction. Broad arbitrary-transition recoding bounds remain open.
proved_step: statement: For every m>=2, integer u with 0<=u<m, and a in Z_m, the transition x -> ux+a mod m on valid binary encodings x in {0,...,m-1} has a total extension to S=ceil(log2 m) output bits computed by O(S^2) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and wires free. Proof: On any S-bit input x, compute z=ux+a using shift-and-add multiplication by the fixed constant u and binary addition; since u< m<=2^S and x<2^S, z has O(S) bits and this takes O(S^2) gates. Reduce z modulo m by binary long division: process its O(S) bits from most significant to least, maintaining an S-bit remainder r; at each step form 2r+b, compare it with the fixed m, and conditionally subtract m. Each step uses O(S) fan-in-two gates, so all steps use O(S^2). The resulting remainder lies in [0,m-1], hence fits in S bits and equals ux+a mod m. This defines outputs on every S-bit input, so in particular is a total extension and is correct on every valid state. The bound is uniform in m,u,a. This proves a polylogarithmic circuit upper bound for modular affine transitions; it does not bound arbitrary transition maps or establish a lower bound.

statement: Explicit modular-affine circuit construction. For m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), 0<=u<m, and a in {0,...,m-1}, there is a total function F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S computed by at most C S^2 fan-in-two AND/NOT gates for an absolute constant C, such that F(x)=ux+a mod m for every S-bit input interpreted as an integer. Proof: Write u=sum_{i=0}^{S-1}u_i2^i. Form the at most S shifted words 2^i x for which u_i=1 and add them, together with constant a, using ripple-carry adders of width at most 2S+1. Each ripple adder uses O(S) gates: XOR is implementable with a constant number of AND/NOT gates, each sum bit uses two XORs, and each carry bit is a constant-size majority circuit. There are at most S additions, so this stage costs O(S^2). Also ux+a<2^(2S)+2^S<2^(2S+1), so z=ux+a has at most 2S+1 bits. Reduce z modulo m by scanning its bits from most significant to least. Start with r=0. For each next bit b form t=2r+b. If 0<=r<m, then 0<=t<2m. Compare t with the hardwired constant m, compute d=t-m by ripple subtraction, and select d if t>=m and t otherwise. Comparison, subtraction, and bitwise selection each use O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates; the selected remainder remains in [0,m-1]. There are at most 2S+1 scanned bits, so reduction costs O(S^2). The recurrence computes the scanned prefix modulo m, hence the final r is z mod m and fits in S bits. Every operation is a Boolean circuit defined on every S-bit input, so their composition is a total S-bit map; for each input integer x it outputs ux+a mod m. The constants u,a,m are hardwired, and the gate-bound constant is absolute.

For every m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), and every directed m-cycle delta on Q, there is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S whose induced transition extends to an S-output fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of O(S) gates. Proof: identify cycle positions with j=0,...,m-1 and encode j in S-bit binary, least significant bit first. The binary incrementer has y_0=NOT x_0 and y_r=x_r XOR c_r, where c_r is the conjunction of the lower r input bits; all c_r are computed by shared prefix conjunctions in O(S) gates, and each XOR has constant AND/NOT cost. Let e(x) be the conjunction specifying the codeword m-1, using O(S) gates, and define F_r(x)=y_r AND NOT e(x). For encoded j<m-1, e=0 and F is j+1; for encoded j=m-1, e=1 and F is 0. Thus F agrees with the cycle on every used codeword. The same circuit defines values on unused codewords. This direct proof includes the non-power-of-two wraparound case.

statement: For every integer m>=2 and every directed m-cycle delta on a set Q, with S=ceil(log_2 m), there is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computable by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and wires free. Proof: Identify Q with residues 0,...,m-1 in cycle order and encode each residue by its S-bit binary representation, least significant bit first. Compute ordinary increment bits y_0=NOT x_0 and y_j=x_j XOR c_j, where c_1=x_0 and c_{j+1}=c_j AND x_j. The shared carry chain uses O(S) gates, since XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. Let e(x) be the conjunction of literals asserting x=m-1; it costs O(S) gates. Define F_j(x)=y_j AND NOT e(x). On each encoded v<m-1, e=0, so F is binary v+1; at v=m-1, e=1, so every output is zero, the encoding of the cycle successor 0. Thus F agrees with the cycle transition on all m encoded states. Its formula defines values on unused words too, giving a total extension with O(S) gates.

statement_start: LEMMA: Cyclic successor on the standard S-bit encoding, S=ceil(log2 m), has a fan-in-2 circuit of size O(S).
evidence: For valid x in [0,m), compute y=x+1 mod 2^S and e=[x=m-1]. Output z_i=y_i AND NOT e for each bit. A fan-in-2 incrementer, equality test against a constant, and output masking each use O(S) gates. For x<m-1 this gives x+1; for x=m-1 it gives 0. Thus the circuit implements cyclic successor on valid encodings in O(S)=O(log m) gates. This proves only an upper bound for the standard encoding.

Arbitrary-length single-cycle encoding lemma. For every integer m>=2, let S=ceil(log2 m), let Q be an m-element set, and let delta be a directed cycle on Q. There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi∘delta∘psi^{-1}, defined on psi(Q), extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computable by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free.

Proof. List Q in cycle order as q_0,...,q_{m-1}, so delta(q_i)=q_{i+1 mod m}. Encode q_i by the S-bit binary representation of i, with bit 0 least significant. These codes are distinct because 0<=i<m<=2^S. For input x, let y be x+1 modulo 2^S. Compute y_0=NOT x_0 and, for j>=1, y_j=x_j XOR c_j, where c_j is the conjunction x_0 AND ... AND x_{j-1}. All carries are computed with the shared recurrence c_1=x_0 and c_{j+1}=c_j AND x_j, using O(S) gates; each XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation, so all y bits cost O(S). Let e(x) be the equality indicator for x=m-1, computed as the conjunction of the S literals matching the binary representation of m-1; this costs O(S) gates. Define F_j(x)=y_j AND NOT e(x) for each output bit j. This adds O(S) gates. If x encodes q_i with i<m-1, then e(x)=0 and y is the binary representation of i+1, so F(x)=psi(q_{i+1}). If x encodes q_{m-1}, then e(x)=1 and F(x)=0=psi(q_0). Thus F agrees with the encoded cycle on every valid code. Its values on unused codes are immaterial, and the displayed formulas define a total Boolean map. The total gate count is O(S).

statement: Equal-length cycle encoding when the bit widths add exactly. Let m>=2 and d>=2 divide m, put t=m/d, and assume ceil(log2 t)+ceil(log2 d)=ceil(log2 m)=S. If delta is a permutation of an m-element set Q whose cycles all have length d, then some injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S makes psi delta psi^{-1} extend to an S-bit Boolean map computed with O(log m) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: Label Q by (i,j), where 0<=i<t identifies the cycle and 0<=j<d its phase, so delta(i,j)=(i,j+1 mod d). Encode i in ceil(log2 t) high bits and j in ceil(log2 d) low bits. The width assumption makes this an S-bit injection. Leave the high output bits unchanged. For the low bits, compute binary j+1 using shared prefix carries, using O(ceil(log2 d)) gates; test whether the low bits equal d-1 using O(ceil(log2 d)) gates, and on that test output zero in every low coordinate, otherwise output the incremented bits. The equality test, shared across coordinates, and each conditional output bit have constant fan-in-two AND/NOT cost per bit (XOR is expressible with constant cost in this basis). On every encoded state with j<d-1 the output is (i,j+1); for j=d-1 it is (i,0). Thus the map agrees with the conjugated transition on psi(Q). Its values on unused codes are supplied by the same circuit. Since ceil(log2 d)<=log2 m, the size is O(log m). This covers d=1 separately by the identity map, with zero gates.

statement: Transposition circuit under any stationary encoding. Let m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), Q be an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and delta:Q->Q swap two distinct states a,b while fixing every other state. Then psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computable by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: Put u=psi(a), v=psi(b), and D={j:u_j!=v_j}. Let e_u(x) be the conjunction of the S literals specifying x=u, and define e_v similarly. For every coordinate j, set F_j(x)=x_j XOR ((e_u(x) OR e_v(x)) AND [j in D]). Equality tests e_u,e_v share input negations and cost O(S) gates total; forming the OR and each of the S conditional toggles costs O(S) further gates, since XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. For x=u or v, exactly one equality indicator is 1, so the coordinates in D toggle and all others stay fixed, giving F(u)=v and F(v)=u. For any other encoded state x=psi(q), injectivity makes both indicators 0, so F(x)=x=psi(delta(q)). The same formula defines F on unused codewords, proving the extension claim.

statement: Sparse-change extension for arbitrary maps. Let m≥2, S=ceil(log₂m), Q be an m-element set, ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective, and δ:Q→Q be any function that differs from the identity on exactly t states. Then ψ∘δ∘ψ⁻¹ on ψ(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computed by O(S+tS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: For each changed state q, form e_q(x), the conjunction of the S literals specifying ψ(q). These indicators together cost O(tS) gates, including shared input negations. For each output coordinate j, let D_j={q:δ(q)≠q and ψ(q)_j≠ψ(δ(q))_j}, and define F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q∈D_j} e_q(x)), taking an empty OR to be 0. Fan-in-two AND/NOT circuits implement each OR term and XOR with constant overhead per term, so the total cost across coordinates is O(S+Σ_j|D_j|)⊆O(S+tS). On an encoded unchanged state every indicator is 0, so F fixes it. On an encoded changed state ψ(q), injectivity makes e_q the sole active indicator, so precisely the coordinates that differ between ψ(q) and ψ(δ(q)) toggle; hence F(ψ(q))=ψ(δ(q)). The same formulas define F on unused codes. No injectivity or surjectivity of δ is used.

statement: Trie-shared sparse-transition extension. Let m≥2, S=ceil(log₂m), Q have m elements, ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective, and δ:Q→Q differ from identity on a set D of size t. Let T be the number of non-root nodes in the binary prefix trie of the S-bit words {ψ(q):q∈D}, including leaves, and let H=Σ_{q∈D} d_H(ψ(q),ψ(δ(q))). Then ψδψ⁻¹ on ψ(Q) has a total S-bit extension with a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of O(S+T+H) gates (constants and wires free). Proof: Set the root indicator to 1. For every trie node v extending its parent by bit b at coordinate k, compute I_v=I_parent AND x_k if b=1, and I_v=I_parent AND NOT x_k if b=0. Compute each NOT x_k once. This constructs all node indicators in at most T+S gates. For each changed q, the leaf indicator I_q is 1 exactly at x=ψ(q); distinct leaves are mutually exclusive. For output coordinate j, let D_j={q∈D: ψ(q)_j≠ψ(δ(q))_j} and define F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q∈D_j} I_q(x)), with an empty OR equal to 0. Binary OR trees and constant-size AND/NOT XOR circuits cost O(S+Σ_j|D_j|)=O(S+H) gates. At x=ψ(q) for changed q, only its leaf is active, so exactly the coordinates differing between ψ(q) and ψ(δ(q)) toggle. At an encoded unchanged q, no changed-state leaf is active, so F fixes ψ(q). Thus F agrees with ψδψ⁻¹ on every valid code and is already defined on unused codes. The total cost is O(S+T+H).

statement: Power-support transition lemma. Let Q be a finite set of size m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), let psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and let delta:Q->Q differ from the identity on at most t states. For every k>=0, psi delta^k psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computable by O((kt+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates.
proof: If delta^k(q) != q, some state among q,delta(q),...,delta^{k-1}(q) is moved by delta; otherwise all iterates in that segment are fixed and delta^k(q)=q. Thus supp(delta^k) is contained in the union of k inverse images of supp(delta), so its size is at most kt. Apply the sparse-change identity-extension construction: form an S-literal equality indicator for each changed encoded state, then for each output bit toggle the input bit by the OR of indicators for changed states whose image changes that bit. Equality indicators cost O(S+|supp(delta^k)|S) total, and OR/XOR formulas cost O(S+|supp(delta^k)|S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. This agrees on every encoded state, with arbitrary outputs on unused codes. For k=0 use the identity map.

statement: Power support containment and encoding lemma. Let Q be finite, let delta:Q->Q, and let supp(delta)={q:delta(q) != q}. For every integer k>=0, supp(delta^k) is a subset of supp(delta). Consequently, for m=|Q|>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), and every injective psi:Q->{0,1}^S, the encoded map psi delta^k psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map with O((|supp(delta)|+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, uniformly in k.
proof: If q is outside supp(delta), then delta(q)=q, and induction gives delta^k(q)=q for every k>=0. Thus supp(delta^k) subset supp(delta), so its size is at most t=|supp(delta)|. For each moved encoded state psi(q) with delta^k(q) != q, form its equality indicator e_q(x), a conjunction of the S literals specifying psi(q). For output coordinate j, set F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q:delta^k(q)_j differs from q_j} e_q(x), where the subscript denotes the jth encoded output bit. On any encoded state, injectivity makes exactly its own indicator one if it is in the selected changed set, and all indicators zero otherwise; hence F(psi(q))=psi(delta^k(q)). Each indicator costs O(S) gates and the OR/XOR corrections over all coordinates cost O(S+|supp(delta^k)|S), giving O((t+1)S). Unused codes may take the formula-defined values.

statement: For m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), every m-element Q, injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S, and map delta:Q->Q, the encoded transition psi delta psi^{-1} extends to a total Boolean map computable by O(mS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: For each q in Q build e_q(x), the conjunction testing x=psi(q), with O(S) gates per indicator and shared input negations. For output bit j, OR all e_q for which bit j of psi(delta(q)) is 1, implemented with a binary tree of constant-size AND/NOT OR gates. On x=psi(q), exactly e_q is 1 by injectivity, so the output is psi(delta(q)); on unused encodings every indicator is 0, defining output 0^S. Total size is O(mS).

evidence: Verified the combinatorial argument: if F|A is bijective, A must be a union of full cycles of F (no tails possible, else first cycle vertex would have two predecessors in A, contradicting injectivity). Cycle type of F|A is exactly the vector (b_i) with 0≤b_i≤a_i and Σ i·b_i = m. The generating function ∏_i (1+z^i+...+z^{a_i i}) coefficient [z^m] counts such vectors exactly. Each vector is a partition of m, so count ≤ p(m). Checked with small examples (e.g., F with a_1=2, a_2=1: m=2 gives 2 types matching p(2)=2; m=3 gives 1 type ≤ p(3)=3). No counterexample found; argument is sound.

Verified the construction: encoding (i,j) as binary(i) concatenated with k-bit binary(j) uses exactly S=ceil(log2(t*2^k)) bits. The transition increments the phase j modulo 2^k while keeping cycle index i fixed. The increment circuit uses shared prefix carries c_1=x_0, c_{j+1}=c_j AND x_j, computing all y_j = x_j XOR (AND_{r<j} x_r) in O(k)=O(log m) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (XOR via AND/NOT/De Morgan). For k=0, delta is identity, zero gates suffice. No counterexample found; the O(log m) bound holds for this permutation subclass.

The proof has an argument gap in the MSB handling. For m not a power of 2, m-1 can have MSB=1 (e.g., m=5, S=3, m-1=4=100). The binary increment of 100 is 101, so y_{S-1}=1, not 0. The proof claims 'y_{S-1} is 0 when x=m-1 anyway since m-1 < 2^S-1 unless m is a power of 2' - this is false when 2^{S-1} < m < 2^S. The construction only applies F_j = y_j AND NOT e(x) for j < S-1, leaving the MSB uncorrected. If implemented as written, F(m-1) would have MSB=1 instead of 0. The lemma can be repaired by applying AND NOT e(x) uniformly to all S output bits (adding one AND and sharing NOT e), keeping O(S) gate count. But the proof as written contains a concrete error.

Verified the construction: encoding states as indices 0..m-1 in binary, using increment modulo 2^S with shared prefix carries (O(S) gates), and correcting at cycle endpoints (c endpoints, each indicator costs O(S), total O(cS)). XOR corrections per output bit cost O(cS). At non-endpoints, increment gives successor; at endpoints, correction redirects to cycle start. The construction is explicit and the gate count O((c+1)S) is correct. No counterexample found; argument is sound.

This is a refinement of S0572/S0611. The bound O(S + tS + h) improves O(S + tS) when the total Hamming displacement h is smaller than tS. The construction is similar: indicators e_q for each of the t changed states (O(tS) gates), then for each output bit j, correct using OR of e_q for q where bit j differs. The total number of such differences across all q is exactly h, so the output corrections cost O(h + S) instead of O(tS + S). Combined: O(tS + h + S). This is a valid refinement. No counterexample found; argument survives review.

Verified the construction: for each changed state q, indicator e_q(x) = conjunction of S literals matching psi(q) costs O(S) gates. Total indicator cost O(tS). For each output bit j, F_j(x) = x_j XOR (OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x)) where D_j = {q: delta(q) != q and bit j differs}. XOR and OR have constant-cost fan-in-two AND/NOT implementations. Total output correction cost O(sum |D_j| + S) = O(tS + S). Correctness: on psi(q) with delta(q)=q, all e_q=0 so F returns psi(q); on psi(q) with delta(q)!=q, injectivity ensures e_q=1 and others 0, toggling exactly differing bits. m=1 edge case handled separately. Argument is sound.

Verified the construction: indicators e_q are conjunctions of S literals (S-1 AND gates each, plus S shared NOT gates for input negations) = t(S-1)+S gates. For each output j, OR of |D_j| indicators via De Morgan: compute NOT e_q for q in D_j (|D_j| NOTs), AND tree (|D_j|-1 ANDs), final NOT (1 gate) = 2|D_j| gates per coordinate. XOR with x_j using (x_j AND NOT OR_j) OR (NOT x_j AND OR_j) = 3 gates per coordinate (all literals available). Total: (tS + S - t) + 2*sum|D_j| + 3S <= 3tS + 4S (since sum|D_j| <= tS). Absolute constant c=7 works for t>=1; t=0 gives identity (0 gates). No argument gap found; construction is explicit and correct for fan-in-two AND/NOT circuits with input wires/constants free.

Verified the construction: identical to S0611/S0572 with explicit gate count. Indicators e_q: t(S-1) AND + S shared NOT = tS + S - t gates. Per output j: OR via De Morgan costs 2|D_j| gates, XOR costs 3 gates (all literals available). Total: tS + S - t + 2*sum|D_j| + 3S <= 3tS + 4S. Absolute constant c=7 works. Construction is sound for fan-in-two AND/NOT with input wires/constants free. No refutation found.

Verified the construction: given reference circuit H of size C computing psi∘f∘psi^{-1} on psi(Q). For t exceptional states where f(q)≠g(q), build indicators e_q(x) = ∧_{r=1}^S l_{q,r}(x) where l_{q,r} is x_r or ¬x_r matching psi(q). Cost: t(S-1) AND + S shared NOT = tS + S - t gates. For each output j, D_j = {q: f(q)≠g(q) and psi_j(f(q))≠psi_j(g(q))}. Correction: F_j(x) = H_j(x) XOR (∨_{q∈D_j} e_q(x)). OR via De Morgan: 2|D_j| gates, XOR: 3 gates (literals available). Total correction: 2∑|D_j| + 3S ≤ 2tS + 3S. Combined circuit: H plus correction layer, size C + O(tS). Correctness: on psi(q) with f(q)=g(q), all e_q=0, F=H=psi∘g∘psi^{-1}; on exceptional psi(q), only e_q=1, toggling exactly changed output bits. No argument gap found. Conditional on H's existence, the bound is sound for fan-in-two AND/NOT with input wires/constants free.

The step incorrectly concludes the lemma is not established for arbitrary involutions. The claimed capacity issue (fixed points exceeding prefix 0 capacity) is resolved by a better encoding: assign the p transpositions to prefixes 0,1,...,p-1 (using both phase bits per prefix), and assign the f fixed points to the remaining prefixes p, p+1, ... (using one or both phase bits as needed). Total prefixes needed: p + ceil(f/2) <= p + f/2 + 0.5 = m/2 + 0.5 <= 2^{S-1} since m <= 2^S. The circuit: on input (y,b) with y in {0,1}^{S-1}, b in {0,1}, if y < p then output (y, b XOR 1) else output (y, b). The comparison y < p is a threshold function on S-1 bits, computable with O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (via binary adder tree). Conditional toggle is O(1) gates. Total O(S) gates. The original lemma statement is TRUE; the step's self-refutation is based on a suboptimal proof strategy, not an actual flaw in the lemma.

Verified the construction: choose any (S-1)-bit string u, assign swapped states to u0 and u1, assign fixed states injectively to the remaining 2^S-2 strings (possible since m <= 2^S). Define F(y,b) = (y, b XOR 1) if y = u, else (y, b). The equality test y = u is a conjunction of S-1 literals (S-2 AND gates + S-1 shared NOTs = O(S) gates). The conditional toggle on the last bit uses O(1) gates per output coordinate (XOR with the equality indicator). Total circuit size O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. The construction is explicit, correct, and the mathematical claim is true. The commentary about 'repairing an overbroad claim' reflects the author's mistaken belief that the general involution lemma fails, but does not affect the correctness of this special case.

Verified the constructive proof: given any injection psi and involution delta with p transpositions, let E be the 2p moved states. For each q in E, construct indicator e_q(x) = 1 iff x = psi(q) as conjunction of S literals (S-1 fan-in-2 AND gates per indicator, using free input literals). Total indicator cost: p(S-1) = O(pS) AND gates. For each output coordinate j, let D_j = {q in E: psi_j(q) != psi_j(delta(q))}. Define F_j(x) = x_j XOR OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x). Since psi is injective, at most one e_q is 1 on any input. OR of |D_j| terms uses max(0, |D_j|-1) fan-in-2 OR gates (each = 1 AND + 2 free NOTs via De Morgan). XOR uses 3 AND gates with free NOTs. Sum_j |D_j| <= pS (each moved state contributes to at most S coordinates). Total gates: indicators p(S-1) + ORs <= pS + XORs 3S = O(pS) for p>=1. On psi(Q), F agrees with psi delta psi^{-1}; on unused codes, F is identity. Construction is explicit, correct, and the asymptotic bound holds.

Verified the constructive proof: partition Q into p transposed pairs and r=m-2p fixed points. Use S-bit codes as (y,b) with y in {0,1}^{S-1}, b in {0,1}. Assign pairs to fibers y=0..p-1 using both phases (y,0) and (y,1). Assign fixed points to remaining codes, needing at most ceil(r/2) additional fibers. Total fibers = p+ceil(r/2) = ceil(m/2) <= 2^{S-1}, so assignment fits. Define F(y,b) = (y, b XOR [y < p]). This swaps each pair and fixes each fixed-point code. A binary comparator y < p against constant p uses O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (process bits MSB to LSB, maintaining 'prefix equal' and 'prefix less' predicates; constant p allows hardwired optimization). The XOR for the last bit uses O(1) gates. Input wires and constants are free per model. The construction is explicit, correct, and achieves O(S) gate bound.

The construction describes a total extension F of psi∘delta∘psi^{-1} on psi(Q) using O(S+tS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates; the gate‑count derivation (indicator costs, OR via De Morgan, XOR) appears consistent, and no counterexample or obvious gap was identified in a brief inspection. The claimed O(t log m + log m) bound follows from the stated component costs.

Verified construction with concrete examples: m=6,p=2,r=2; m=5,p=2,r=1; m=7,p=3,r=1. The construction assigns transposed pairs (q2k, q2k+1) to fibers y=0,...,p-1 with codes (y,0),(y,1), and assigns remaining elements to fibers y>=p. The function F(y,b)=(y,b XOR [y<p)) correctly swaps bits for transposed pairs (y<p) and fixes bits for fixed points (y>=p). The injection property holds as each element gets a distinct code. Total fibers used: p + ceil(r/2) where r=m-2p, which satisfies p+ceil(r/2) <= 2^(S-1) by the inequality ceil(m/2) <= 2^(ceil(log2 m)-1).

Verified with example X={0,1,2,3}, F=(0→1→0)(2→3→2). Computed both direct count (m=0:1, m=1:0, m=2:2, m=3:0, m=4:1) and formula [z^m](1+z^2)^2, matching exactly. The combinatorial argument is sound: F|A bijective implies A is union of complete cycles, and conversely.

Verified with X={0,1,2,3}, F=(0→1→0)(2→3→2). Computed both direct count (m=0:1, m=1:0, m=2:2, m=3:0, m=4:1) and formula [z^m](1+z²)², matching exactly. The combinatorial argument is sound: F|A bijective implies A is union of complete cycles, and conversely.
Verified for X={0,1,2,3}, F=(0→1→0)(2→3→2): m=0:1✓, m=1:0✓, m=2:2✓, m=3:0✓, m=4:1✓. Proof logic correct: F|A bijective implies A is union of full cycles.

proved_step: statement: Sparse-support extension bound. Let m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), Q be an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective, and delta:Q->Q any map. Put T={q:delta(q)!=q}, and h_q=Hamming(psi(q),psi(delta(q))). There is a total S-bit Boolean map extending psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q), with fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit size O(S + S|T| + sum_{q in T} h_q). Proof: For every q in T form e_q(x)=1 iff x=psi(q), an S-literal conjunction, using shared input negations; total cost O(S|T|). For each output coordinate j form z_j as the OR of e_q over those q in T whose encoded successor differs at bit j (empty OR is zero), then output x_j XOR z_j. Across coordinates the OR trees cost O(sum_j |D_j| + S)=O(sum_q h_q+S), and the XORs cost O(S). At x=psi(q), injectivity makes exactly e_q active among T if q is nonfixed; if q is fixed no indicator is active and output is x. Thus each coordinate flips exactly when its successor coordinate differs, giving psi(delta(q)). At inputs outside psi(Q) the formulas still define a total map. Summing costs gives the stated bound. This corrects the unsupported O(S+sum h_q) bound but does not imply a lower bound or an online reconstruction result.

statement: Sparse-support extension bound (corrected). Let m≥2, S=ceil(log2 m), Q be an m-element set, ψ:Q→{0,1}^S injective, and δ:Q→Q. Set T={q:δ(q)≠q} and h_q=Hamming(ψ(q),ψ(δ(q))). The map ψδψ⁻¹ on ψ(Q) has a total Boolean extension computed by O(S+S|T|+Σ_{q∈T}h_q) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: For each q∈T, compute e_q(x)=[x=ψ(q)] using an S-literal conjunction; shared input negations and these conjunctions cost O(S|T|+S). For each output coordinate j, let D_j={q∈T:ψ(q)_j≠ψ(δ(q))_j}, and set F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q∈D_j}e_q(x)), with empty OR equal to 0. Fan-in-two OR trees and XOR implementations cost O(Σ_j|D_j|+S)=O(Σ_q h_q+S). If x=ψ(q) and q∈T, injectivity makes e_q the only active indicator, so precisely the coordinates that differ are flipped. If q∉T, all indicators are zero and F(x)=x=ψ(δ(q)). The formulas define F on every input, giving a total extension. This repairs the earlier unsupported O(S+Σh_q) claim by accounting for equality-test cost. It does not prove a lower bound or close the online recoding gap.

evidence: The claimed O(S+sum_{q in T} h_q) gate bound is not established and the step's own construction yields only O(S+S·sum h_q): an equality indicator for a changed state requires testing S input literals, and it must be formed for each state/changed output pair unless shared. The proposed separate-indicator construction explicitly incurs O(S·sum h_q), contradicting the claimed additive bound. This refutes the stated proof/claim as written, not the possibility of a stronger construction.

gap: The Hamming-displacement extension bound O(S+sum h_q) in S0626 remains open; the repair only gives a general truth-table extension bound O(S^2·2^S).
evidence: The minterm construction is exact on every encoded state and defines arbitrary values elsewhere. There are S output bits, each with at most 2^S minterms, each using O(S) literals and O(2^S) OR gates, giving O(S^2·2^S) total. Since 2^S<2m and S=ceil(log2 m), this is O(m(log m)^2).
proved_step: REPAIR LEMMA (GENERAL TABLE EXTENSION). For every injective encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^S, |Q|=m, and every map δ:Q→Q, the induced partial map ψ(q)↦ψ(δ(q)) has a total Boolean extension on S bits with O(S·2^S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, hence O(m log m) gates when S=ceil(log2 m). Proof: For each output coordinate j, write its truth table as a disjunction of minterms, one minterm for every x∈{0,1}^S on which the required output bit is 1, assigning arbitrary outputs on unused codes. Each minterm is a conjunction of S literals and costs at most S−1 binary AND gates after input negations are shared. The OR of at most 2^S minterms costs at most 2^S−1 binary OR gates, with OR implemented by De Morgan using AND and NOT. Thus each output bit costs O(S·2^S), and all S outputs cost O(S^2·2^S), not O(S·2^S). Consequently the valid bound proved here is O(S^2·2^S)=O(m(log m)^2), which repairs the false additive-displacement claim with a general exact upper bound.

TRIE-SHARED TRANSITION EXTENSION LEMMA. Let Q have m>=2 states, let S=ceil(log2 m), let ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective, and let δ:Q→Q change exactly t states. Let T be the set of their S-bit encodings. Form the binary prefix trie of T, with the root omitted and unary and branching prefix nodes counted; let L be its number of nodes. Put H=Σ_{q:δ(q)≠q} d_H(ψ(q),ψ(δ(q))). Then the encoded partial map has a total Boolean extension using O(S+L+H) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Share the negations of the S input bits. For each trie node, compute its prefix-match indicator from its parent indicator and the next matching literal, using one AND gate; the root indicator is 1. Each changed state q has a leaf indicator e_q, equal to 1 exactly at ψ(q), because ψ is injective and the leaves are distinct. For each output bit j, collect the leaves q for which ψ(q)_j differs from ψ(δ(q))_j. Define output j as x_j XOR the OR of their indicators (empty OR is 0). The ORs and XORs use O(1) gates per leaf occurrence, for O(H) total; the trie uses O(L) gates. At an unchanged encoded state no changed leaf indicator is active, so the output is ψ(q). At a changed encoded state exactly its leaf indicator is active, so precisely the differing destination bits are toggled. The formulas define outputs on every unused code, giving a total extension. Thus the cost is O(S+L+H). For a full trie L can be Θ(St), so this does not establish O(S+H) in general; it isolates the remaining obstacle as bounding shared prefix complexity for a useful encoding.

proved_step: statement: CONSTANT-IMAGE TRANSITION LEMMA. Let Q be a finite set, ψ:Q→{0,1}^S any injection, and δ:Q→Q have image of size one, say δ(q)=q_* for every q∈Q. Then ψ∘δ∘ψ^{-1} on ψ(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computed with zero fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (constants are free). Proof: Define F(x)=ψ(q_*) for every x∈{0,1}^S. Each of its S output coordinates is the corresponding constant bit of ψ(q_*), hence needs no gates under the stipulated free-constants convention. For every q∈Q, F(ψ(q))=ψ(q_*)=ψ(δ(q)), so F is the required extension. This holds for every stationary injective encoding and all S, including S=0. The result isolates the constant-map boundary case; it gives no bound for image size at least two.

gap: This establishes a universal constructive upper bound in an expanded one-hot representation only. It does not close the assigned minimum-width stationary recoding obligations or open bridge D; those remain open.
proved_step: statement: ONE-HOT UNIVERSAL TRANSITION UPPER BOUND. For every m>=1, every map delta:Q->{0,1}^Q on an m-element set has an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^m such that the encoded transition extends to a total map on {0,1}^m computed by at most m^2+m fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (input wires and constants are free). Proof: Enumerate Q={q_1,...,q_m} and encode q_i by the unit vector e_i. For each output coordinate j, let P_j={i: delta(q_i)=q_j}, and define F_j(x)=OR_{i in P_j} x_i, with the empty OR equal to 0. Implement each OR as a binary tree of OR gates; OR(a,b)=NOT(AND(NOT a,NOT b)), costing three allowed gates per internal node. The total number of internal nodes over all j is sum_j max(|P_j|-1,0) <= sum_j |P_j|=m, so this implementation uses at most 3m gates, which is <=m^2+m for m>=1. At x=e_i, exactly one input indicator is 1, hence F(e_i)=e_k where q_k=delta(q_i). Thus F is a total extension and the encoding is injective. Diagnostic: the construction uses m state bits, not S=ceil(log2 m), and gives no lower bound or P-vs-NP implication.

gap: The corrected universal upper bound uses one-hot width m. The assigned minimum-width recoding bounds and time-dependent/amortized bridge D remain open; S0681's m^2+m bound had an invalid m=1 comparison, repaired here by stating the valid 3m bound directly.
proved_step: statement: CORRECTED ONE-HOT UNIVERSAL TRANSITION UPPER BOUND. For every integer m>=1 and every map delta:Q->{0,1}^Q on an m-element set, there is an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^m such that the encoded transition extends to a total Boolean map computed by at most 3m fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with input wires and constants free. Proof: Enumerate Q={q_1,...,q_m} and encode q_i by the unit vector e_i. For each j define P_j={i:delta(q_i)=q_j} and F_j(x)=OR_{i in P_j} x_i, taking an empty OR to be 0. For |P_j|>=2 implement this OR by a binary tree with |P_j|-1 OR gates; implement each OR(a,b) as NOT(AND(NOT a,NOT b)), costing three allowed gates. For |P_j|=1 the output is a wire, and for |P_j|=0 it is a free constant, so the total gate count is at most 3 sum_j |P_j|=3m. At x=e_i exactly one input bit is 1, so F(x)=e_k for q_k=delta(q_i). Thus F is a total extension agreeing with the encoded transition on every code. This uses m state bits, not ceil(log2 m), and asserts no lower bound or P-vs-NP consequence.

gap: The image-sensitive one-hot bound refines the universal m-bit upper bound but does not close or shrink the minimum-width stationary recoding bounds or bridge D for time-dependent/one-to-many encodings; those remain open.
proved_step: statement: IMAGE-SENSITIVE ONE-HOT TRANSITION UPPER BOUND. Let m>=1, let Q be an m-element set and delta:Q->Q, and let r=|delta(Q)|. Under the encoding psi(q_i)=e_i in {0,1}^m, the encoded transition has a total Boolean extension using at most 3(m-r) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with input wires and constants free. Proof: For each q_j in delta(Q), put k_j=|delta^{-1}(q_j)|>=1 and define output bit j to be OR_{i:delta(q_i)=q_j} x_i; for q_j outside delta(Q), use constant zero. An OR of k_j inputs uses k_j-1 binary OR gates, each implemented using three AND/NOT gates. Since the nonempty preimages partition Q, sum_{j in delta(Q)} k_j=m, so total gates are 3 sum_j(k_j-1)=3(m-r). On input e_i exactly one input bit is one, and the output is e_j for q_j=delta(q_i), proving extension correctness. This uses m state bits and does not assert a minimum-width or lower-bound result.

lemma: For every m-state function and every injective S-bit encoding, there is a total transition extension of size O(mS), by decoding each encoded state once and sharing its indicator across output coordinates.
proved_step: statement: Explicit minterm extension for arbitrary encoded transitions. Let m>=1, S=ceil(log2 m), Q be an m-element set, delta:Q->Q any function, and psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective. There exists a total Boolean map F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S agreeing with psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q), computed with O(mS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with input wires and constants free. For each q in Q, form e_q(x) as the conjunction of the S literals specifying x=psi(q), using S-1 binary AND gates when S>=1; share this indicator across all output coordinates. For each coordinate j, set F_j(x)=OR_{q: psi(delta(q))_j=1} e_q(x); a binary OR is implemented from AND/NOT by De Morgan, and the OR uses at most m-1 gates. At x=psi(q), injectivity gives e_q=1 and every other e_r=0, hence F_j(psi(q))=psi(delta(q))_j. The formulas define F on unused codes, whose values are unrestricted. The total gate count is at most m(S-1)+S(m-1)=O(mS). If S=0 then m=1 and the unique output is the zero-bit map, requiring no gates.

proved_step: statement: GENERIC TOTAL-EXTENSION SYNTHESIS LEMMA. Let Q be an m-element set, m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), let psi:Q->{0,1}^S be any injection, and let delta:Q->Q be any function. There is a total Boolean map F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S extending psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q), computed with O(mS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (input wires and constants free). Proof: For each q in Q form the minterm e_q(x)=AND_{i=1}^S l_{q,i}(x), where l_{q,i}=x_i if psi(q)_i=1 and NOT x_i otherwise. Compute all input negations once and all minterms with at most S-1 binary AND gates each, for O(mS) gates. For output coordinate j, set T_j={q: psi(delta(q))_j=1} and define F_j=OR_{q in T_j} e_q, using at most max(|T_j|-1,0) binary OR gates, each implementable with a constant number of AND/NOT gates. Summed over j this costs O(mS). On input psi(q), injectivity makes exactly e_q equal 1, so F_j(psi(q))=psi(delta(q))_j. The formulas define F on unused codes as well. This gives an explicit upper bound for every injection and transition, but does not establish the sharper O(sqrt(m) polylog m) bound for a choice of encoding.

statement: SPARSE-CHANGES EXTENSION LEMMA. Let |Q|=m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), and let psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective. If delta:Q->Q fixes all but t states, then psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map using O((t+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with input wires and constants free. Proof: Let A={q:delta(q)!=q}. For each q in A, construct e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] by ANDing its S matching literals, sharing input negations. This costs O(S|A|). For bit j, let D_j={q in A: psi(q)_j!=psi(delta(q))_j}; define F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x). Binary trees implement each OR, and OR and XOR each have constant-size AND/NOT implementations. Since sum_j |D_j|<=S|A|, the total cost is O(S(t+1)). At an encoded fixed state all indicators vanish, so F_j=x_j. At an encoded changed state, injectivity makes only its indicator active, so F toggles precisely the bits differing between source and destination. Thus F agrees with the transition on psi(Q), and its formulas define a total map on all bit strings. For t=0 use the identity map. This improves the generic O(mS) synthesis bound when t=o(m), but does not establish the worst-case recoding bounds.

statement: INTERVAL ENCODING FOR A c-CYCLE PERMUTATION. For every m>=2 and permutation delta on an m-element set with c cycles, there is an injection psi into {0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), such that psi delta psi^{-1} extends to a total Boolean map computed by O(cS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Order the cycles and list each cycle consecutively. Let cycle i occupy [a_i,b_i] in the integer codes 0,...,m-1, with successor x+1 except b_i maps to a_i. Build an S-bit incrementer u(x) at cost O(S). For each endpoint b_i compute e_i(x)=[x=b_i] by an S-literal conjunction, total O(cS). For every output bit j, correct u_j at endpoint b_i to constant (a_i)_j by XORing e_i AND (u_j XOR (a_i)_j); each endpoint-bit correction costs O(1), hence O(cS) total. The endpoint indicators are mutually exclusive. On non-endpoint codes all corrections vanish and output is x+1; at b_i the correction sets the output to a_i. This agrees with delta on every valid code. Define the circuit arbitrarily by the same formula on unused codes; it is a total extension. Thus the encoding and extension have the stated gate bound.

statement: GENERAL TRANSITION EXTENSION BOUND. Let Q be an m-element set, m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), delta:Q->Q any function, and psi:Q->{0,1}^S any injection. Then the encoded transition psi∘delta∘psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S computable by O(mS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: For each q∈Q form e_q(x)=1 iff x=psi(q), as the conjunction of S literals; share input negations and each indicator. For output coordinate j define F_j(x)=OR_{q: psi(delta(q))_j=1} e_q(x), with empty OR equal to 0. Injectivity makes exactly one indicator active at each valid code and none active at unused codes. Thus F agrees with the encoded transition on psi(Q), and is zero on unused codes. The shared equality tests cost O(mS); the S output ORs cost O(mS).
derivation: Singleton equality indicators identify each valid source encoding. Coordinate-wise OR over the indicators whose destination has that bit set produces the transition output. Sharing the indicators gives O(mS) total gates.
gap: Baseline truth-table upper bound only. Does not establish the target Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) lower bound or the sharper encoding upper bound; no P-vs-NP transfer.

statement: HAMMING-CHANGE EXTENSION BOUND. Let Q have m>=2 elements, S=ceil(log2 m), delta:Q->Q, and psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective. Define H=sum_{q in Q} d_H(psi(q),psi(delta(q))). The encoded transition on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map computable with O(S+H) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: For each q form e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] by an S-literal conjunction, sharing input negations. For each output bit j, let D_j={q: psi(q)_j differs from psi(delta(q))_j}, and define F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x)); an empty OR is 0. At a valid encoding psi(q), injectivity makes e_q the only active indicator, so F_j toggles exactly the bits in which psi(q) differs from psi(delta(q)). Hence F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)). On unused codes, the same formulas define F, so this is a total extension. The equality tests cost O(mS). The ORs cost O(sum_j |D_j|)=O(H), and the S XORs cost O(S).
derivation: Use equality indicators to identify each source state, then toggle only the coordinates that differ between its encoding and its successor. The total number of such state-coordinate pairs is exactly H.
gap: This is an encoding-specific upper bound. It does not establish a bound on the minimum over encodings, nor the target lower bound.

For every m>=2 and map delta:Q->Q on |Q|=m, S=ceil(log2 m), there is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi delta psi^{-1} extends to a total S-bit Boolean map using O(mS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: choose distinct S-bit codes a_q. For each q compute e_q(x)=[x=a_q] by an S-literal conjunction; shared negations and all indicators cost O(S+mS). Output bit j is OR of e_q over q whose destination code a_delta(q) has bit j equal to 1, costing at most m-1 binary OR gates per bit. At x=a_q exactly e_q is 1, so each output is the corresponding bit of a_delta(q). At unused codes all indicators are zero, defining a total extension. Total cost O(mS).

For every permutation delta on an m-element set with r cycles, m>=2 and S=ceil(log2 m), there exists an injection psi into {0,1}^S such that the encoded transition extends to a total Boolean map computed by O(rS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: enumerate states consecutively cycle by cycle and encode them by integers 0,...,m-1. The transition is increment modulo 2^S except at each of the r cycle endpoints, where it maps to that cycle's start. Compute u(x)=x+1 modulo 2^S in O(S) gates. For each endpoint a form e_a(x)=[x=a] in O(S) gates. For each output bit j, XOR u_j(x) with the OR of e_a(x) over endpoints where u_j(a) differs from the required start-code bit. This corrects exactly the endpoint outputs and leaves all other valid-code outputs unchanged. Equality tests, ORs, and XORs have fan-in-two AND/NOT implementations, so total size is O(S+rS)=O(rS). The formulas define a total map on all S-bit strings.

statement: Cycle-interval encoding lemma. For every m>=2, every permutation delta of an m-element set Q having k cycles admits an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), such that the encoded transition psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map computed by O(kS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: List the cycles in any order with lengths l_1,...,l_k and let a_1=0, a_i=sum_{h<i} l_h. In cycle i, enumerate states q_{i,0},...,q_{i,l_i-1} in transition order and encode q_{i,j} by the S-bit binary representation of a_i+j. These are distinct integers in [0,m), so psi is injective. Define a circuit on all S-bit inputs x as follows. For each i form the interval indicator I_i(x)=[a_i<=x<a_i+l_i], using two constant-threshold comparisons; each comparison has an O(S)-gate fan-in-two AND/NOT implementation by scanning bits from most significant to least significant and maintaining equal-prefix and already-less flags. Let b_i=a_i+l_i-1. On the interval I_i, the desired output is a_i when x=b_i and x+1 otherwise. Compute the equality flag E_i=[x=b_i] with O(S) literals and AND gates, and compute x+1 modulo 2^S with an O(S)-gate ripple incrementer. For each output bit r, form the selected bit I_i AND ((E_i AND bit_r(a_i)) OR ((NOT E_i) AND bit_r(x+1))). OR, AND, and NOT have constant-size fan-in-two implementations. OR the k selected terms for each output bit. The total cost is O(kS), including all interval tests, endpoint tests, increment logic and output selection. For x outside the union of the intervals, define every output bit to be zero; this is achieved by the same formula, since every I_i is false. For x=a_i+j with j<l_i-1 the formula outputs a_i+j+1; for x=b_i it outputs a_i. Thus it agrees with delta on every encoded state. Diagnostic: this is verified mathematics for the stated circuit model; no transfer to P vs NP is asserted.

statement: Explicit sparse-change extension bound. Let Q have m≥2 elements, S=ceil(log2 m), and ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective. For any map δ:Q→Q that differs from the identity on exactly t states, the encoded transition has a total Boolean extension on S bits using O(S(t+1)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: Let E be the t exceptional encodings. For each a∈E compute e_a(x)=[x=a] by an S-literal conjunction, sharing the S input negations; this costs at most (S−1)t+S gates. For each output coordinate j, let E_j contain those a∈E where ψ(δ(ψ⁻¹(a)))_j differs from a_j. Compute h_j=OR_{a∈E_j}e_a using shared complements ¬e_a, an AND tree, and one final NOT; across all coordinates this costs at most t+St+S gates (empty E_j gives constant 0). Set y_j=x_j XOR h_j. XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation, so all outputs cost O(S). On a valid encoding outside E, every indicator is zero and y=x. On a∈E, injectivity makes exactly e_a active, so h_j=1 exactly on the coordinates that must change; hence y=ψ(δ(ψ⁻¹(a))). The formulas define a total map on all bit strings, and values on unused codes are unconstrained. This gives an explicit gate-count construction and the bound O(S(t+1)); it is an upper bound, not a lower bound or a P-vs-NP result.

statement: Cycle-interval encoding lemma. For every permutation δ of an m-element set, with c cycles and S=ceil(log₂m), there is an injective encoding ψ into {0,1}^S for which the encoded transition extends to a total Boolean map computed by O(S(c+1)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Order the cycles arbitrarily and assign their states consecutive integer codes, keeping each cycle’s states consecutive and in transition order. Thus each cycle occupies an interval [a,b]. For every code x in that interval except b, the transition is x↦x+1. At each of the c interval endpoints b, the desired output is the interval’s start a. On all S-bit strings use the shared binary increment modulo 2^S as a base map. For each endpoint code b, form the equality indicator e_b(x)=[x=b] using S literals. For each output bit j, let E_j contain endpoints where bit j of b+1 mod 2^S differs from bit j of the desired cycle start. XOR the base output bit with OR_{b∈E_j} e_b(x). Equality indicators cost O(Sc); all endpoint ORs together cost O(Sc), and the S incrementer and output XORs cost O(S). At a valid non-endpoint code the correction indicators vanish and increment gives the correct successor. At an endpoint exactly its own indicator is active, changing the base output to the required cycle start. Hence the extension agrees on every encoded state; its behavior on unused codes is unrestricted. For c=o(m), this improves the O(Sm) general encoding bound. The lemma is an upper bound for permutations with few cycles, not a lower bound or a P-vs-NP result.

CYCLE-INTERVAL UPPER-BOUND LEMMA. Let Q be a finite set of size m>=2, let F:Q->Q be a permutation with c cycles, and put S=ceil(log_2 m). There is an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that the encoded transition on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computed by O((c+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: List the cycles in any order. For each cycle i of length l_i, choose a starting offset a_i, with a_1=0 and a_{i+1}=a_i+l_i, and encode its successive states by the S-bit binary codes of a_i,...,a_i+l_i-1. These are distinct integers in [0,m-1], so psi is injective. Let b_i=a_i+l_i-1 be the endpoint code and let y(x)=x+1 modulo 2^S. For each i, define d_i as the S-bit vector (a_i - (b_i+1)) modulo 2^S, and let e_i(x) be the equality indicator [x=b_i]. Define the output vector Fhat(x)=y(x) XOR (XOR over i of (e_i(x) AND d_i)), where the AND with d_i is coordinatewise. For x in psi(Q) that is not an endpoint, all e_i vanish and y(x) is exactly the next code in its cycle. At endpoint b_i, precisely e_i is 1, so the output is (b_i+1)+d_i=a_i modulo 2^S, the code of that cycle's first state. Thus Fhat agrees with the transition on every encoded state; the same formula defines it on every S-bit input. Gate count: y is a binary increment modulo 2^S, computable with O(S) gates using shared prefix-AND carries and constant-size AND/NOT implementations of XOR. Each endpoint equality indicator costs O(S) gates, sharing input negations if desired. For each i, the coordinatewise mask e_i AND d_i costs at most S gates; combining the c masks into the S outputs costs O(cS) two-input XOR implementations. Total O((c+1)S). This is a constructive upper bound only; it makes no lower-bound or P-vs-NP claim and uses no prior claimed proof steps.

statement: Composition bound for sparse encoded transitions. Fix an injective encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^S, |Q|=m≥2, and maps δ_1,...,δ_r:Q→Q, where δ_i changes t_i states. Each encoded map ψδ_iψ^{-1} on ψ(Q) has a total extension C_i of size O(S(1+t_i)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Their composition C_r∘...∘C_1 is a total S-bit circuit of size O(S(r+Σ_i t_i)); on every ψ(q) it equals ψ((δ_r∘...∘δ_1)(q)). Proof: For each δ_i, compute equality indicators e_q=[x=ψ(q)] for changed states q, and for each bit j XOR the OR of those indicators for which ψ(q)_j differs from ψ(δ_i(q))_j. This agrees with δ_i on ψ(Q). Since every δ_i maps Q into Q, induction shows that the composition agrees on ψ(Q). Substituting each circuit’s outputs into the next preserves fan-in two and adds gate counts, proving the bound. Diagnostic: no P≠NP progress is claimed.

statement: Support-union composition lemma. Let Q be a finite set, let δ_1,...,δ_r be permutations of Q, and write supp(δ_i)={q∈Q:δ_i(q)≠q}. Then supp(δ_r∘...∘δ_1)⊆⋃_{i=1}^r supp(δ_i). Consequently, for any injective encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2|Q|), the composite has a total fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit extension of size O(S(1+Σ_i t_i)), where t_i=|supp(δ_i)|. Proof: If q is outside ⋃_i supp(δ_i), every δ_i fixes q. Inductively, after each successive map the state is still q, so the composite fixes q. This proves the support inclusion and bounds the composite support by Σ_i t_i. Apply the sparse-transition construction: for each moved state u of the composite, form its encoding equality indicator [x=ψ(u)] using O(S) gates, and for each output bit XOR the OR of indicators for moved states whose destination bit differs from their source bit. Shared input negations and fan-in-two implementations give O(S(1+t)) gates for t moved states; injectivity ensures exactly the intended indicator is active at each valid moved code, while unchanged codes activate none. The formula defines a total map on all bit strings and agrees with the composite on ψ(Q). Since t≤Σ_i t_i, the asserted bound follows. Diagnostic: this is a recoding-complexity lemma only; it makes no P≠NP claim.

statement: For every permutation delta on an m-element set, m>=2, with S=ceil(log2 m), there exists an injective stationary encoding into {0,1}^S whose encoded transition extends to a total Boolean map of O(sqrt(m) log^2 m) fan-in-two gates. Proof: list each cycle in successor order and allocate consecutive codes to each cycle interval. Let d be the number of distinct cycle lengths; since these lengths are distinct positive integers, d(d+1)/2<=m, hence d<=sqrt(2m). The base map B(x)=x+1 mod 2^S has an O(S)-gate fan-in-two implementation. For each cycle endpoint e with interval start a, compute E_e(x)=[x=e] at cost O(S). For each output bit j use F_j(x)=B_j(x) XOR OR_e(E_e(x) AND (B_j(x) XOR a_j)). Each endpoint correction costs O(S) over all output bits, so total size O((d+1)S^2)=O(sqrt(m) log^2 m). On non-endpoints this is B; at endpoint e exactly its indicator is active and output becomes a, the cycle start. The same formulas define a total map on all codes, including unused codes.

refuted_approach: S0699's unrestricted O(sqrt(m) log^2 m) conclusion is not justified: its interval construction has one endpoint correction per cycle, and the number of distinct cycle lengths does not bound the number of cycles. Corrected scope: c-cycle permutations have an O((c+1)S) encoding bound.
proved_step: statement: For every permutation on m>=2 states having c cycles, with S=ceil(log2 m), there exists an injective stationary encoding into {0,1}^S such that the encoded transition extends to a total Boolean map of O((c+1)S) fan-in-two gates. Proof: list each cycle in successor order and assign its states consecutive integer codes, forming one interval per cycle. Let B(x)=x+1 mod 2^S, computed by an O(S)-gate incrementer. For each cycle endpoint e with interval start a_e, compute E_e(x)=[x=e] using O(S) gates. For each output bit j define F_j(x)=B_j(x) XOR OR_e(E_e(x) AND (B_j(x) XOR (a_e)_j)). The endpoint indicators are mutually exclusive; on non-endpoint codes all corrections vanish, and at endpoint e the formula replaces B(x) by a_e, the required cycle successor. These formulas define a total map on all codes. The incrementer costs O(S); endpoint tests cost O(cS); correction terms and per-bit OR aggregation cost O(cS). Total O((c+1)S).

statement: For every permutation delta on m>=2 states, with S=ceil(log2 m), there is an injective encoding into S bits whose encoded transition extends to a total Boolean map using O(sqrt(m) S^2) fan-in-two gates. Proof: Group cycles by length. For each distinct length l, place all its cycles consecutively in a block, each cycle occupying l codes. There are d<=sqrt(2m) distinct lengths because the sum of those distinct positive integers is at most m. Use B(x)=x+1 mod 2^S as default. For a valid code in the l block, the desired successor is B(x), except at endpoints, identified by offset+1 divisible by l, where it is x-(l-1). Compute each block membership with O(S) gates and its endpoint predicate by a bitwise constant-modulus remainder computation using an O(log l)-bit remainder across S input bits, costing O(S log l) gates. Compute endpoint correction output x-(l-1) with O(S) gates and select it at endpoints. The block predicates are disjoint; combining corrections across d blocks costs O(dS). Total O(d S^2)=O(sqrt(m) S^2). These formulas extend to a total map on all codes, with behavior outside encoded states arbitrary.

Repair candidate: gate each endpoint correction by full interval membership a<=x<b; this adds O(S) gates per length block and preserves the claimed asymptotic if the remaining modular circuit bound is valid.
