proved_step: statement: PERIODIC TIME-VARYING RECODING LEMMA. Let Q be a finite set, let δ:Q→Q be a permutation of finite order L, and let ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be any injection. For each integer t define ψ_t=ψ∘δ^{-t}, with t interpreted modulo L. Then for every q∈Q, ψ_{t+1}(δ(q))=ψ_t(q). Thus each transition from time t to t+1 is the identity on valid encoded states and has a zero-gate implementation; the encoding schedule is periodic with period L. Proof: ψ_{t+1}(δ(q))=ψ(δ^{-(t+1)}(δ(q)))=ψ(δ^{-t}(q))=ψ_t(q). Since δ^L is the identity, ψ_{t+L}=ψ_t. This lemma concerns the transition between changing codebooks; it does not bound the cost of maintaining or synchronizing the time-dependent decoder.

evidence: Applying the same fixed decoder to the assumed code-word equality proves the statement directly. This is independent of the earlier unreviewed stationary-encoding claims and S0703. It formalizes that the time-varying recoding construction must change the decoder for a nonidentity transition; no P-vs-NP transfer is asserted.
proved_step: statement: FIXED-DECODER ZERO-UPDATE OBSTRUCTION. Let Q be a set, δ:Q→Q a map, C a code set, and D:C→Q a fixed decoder. Suppose encodings ψ_t:Q→C satisfy D(ψ_t(q))=q for every t,q, and updates preserve code words: ψ_{t+1}(δ(q))=ψ_t(q). Then δ is the identity. Proof: Apply D to the update equality. Correct decoding at time t+1 gives D(ψ_{t+1}(δ(q)))=δ(q); at time t it gives D(ψ_t(q))=q. The code words are equal, so their decoder outputs are equal, and δ(q)=q. Therefore any nonidentity transition with zero code-word updates requires changing the decoder.

evidence: The proof evaluates each decoder at the single valid code ψ(q_0); it does not rely on unreviewed stationary-encoding claims. It establishes phase storage only, not decoder update cost or circuit complexity.
proved_step: statement: PHASE-DECODER DISTINCTNESS FOR A CYCLE. Let Q={q_0,...,q_{m-1}} with m>=2 and δ(q_j)=q_{j+1 mod m}. Let C be a code set, let ψ:Q→C be injective, and for each t in Z/mZ let D_t:C→Q satisfy D_t(ψ(q_j))=q_{j+t mod m} for every j. Then D_0,...,D_{m-1} are pairwise distinct. Consequently, if the decoder is determined by a phase state z_t through one fixed map H, so D_t=H(z_t), then there are at least m distinct phase states and any binary representation of them needs at least ceil(log2 m) bits. Proof: If D_a=D_b, evaluate both at ψ(q_0): q_a=D_a(ψ(q_0))=D_b(ψ(q_0))=q_b. The cycle states are distinct, so a=b modulo m. Thus the decoders are pairwise distinct. If z_a=z_b, then H(z_a)=H(z_b), hence D_a=D_b and a=b; therefore the phase states are pairwise distinct. B bits encode at most 2^B states, so 2^B>=m and B>=ceil(log2 m).

statement: BOUNDED-SUPPORT EXTENSION WITH EMPTY-SUPPORT BOUNDARY. Let m>=2, S=ceil(log_2 m), Q be an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S be any injection, and delta:Q->Q. If supp(delta)={q:delta(q)!=q} has size t, then the partial map psi(q)->psi(delta(q)) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map with O(S(1+t)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. If t=0 the extension is the identity and uses zero gates. Proof: For every q in supp(delta), let e_q(x) be the conjunction of the S literals specifying psi(q), using shared input negations; all these indicators cost O(St). For each output coordinate j define F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x), where D_j={q in supp(delta): psi(q)_j != psi(delta(q))_j}. A conjunction and each OR can be built with fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, and XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. Sharing all e_q gives total cost O(St+S+sum_j |D_j|)=O(S(1+t)); when t=0 each D_j is empty and F_j=x_j, so no gates are needed. On an encoded unchanged state, every e_q is zero. On an encoded changed state, injectivity ensures exactly its own e_q is one, so each coordinate toggles precisely when source and destination bits differ. Thus F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for every q; values on unused codes are unrestricted. This is a constructive stationary upper bound only, not a representation-independent lower bound.

statement: TRIE-SHARED SPARSE TRANSITION EXTENSION. Let Q have m>=1 elements, S=ceil(log2 m), psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and D={q:delta(q)!=q}, with |D|=t. Let T be the number of non-root nodes in the binary prefix trie of {psi(q):q in D}, and D_j={q in D:psi(q)_j!=psi(delta(q))_j}. A total extension of the encoded transition has a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of size O(S+T+sum_j max(0,|D_j|-1)). Proof: Compute each equality indicator [x=psi(q)] by extending shared prefix conjunctions in the trie, costing O(T) gates and O(S) shared input negations. For each j, OR the indicators for q in D_j, using max(0,|D_j|-1) gates, with empty OR equal to 0. Output bit j as x_j XOR that OR, using constant-size AND/NOT circuits. At unchanged encoded states all indicators vanish. At changed encoded state psi(q), injectivity makes exactly its indicator true, so precisely the differing coordinates toggle and the output is psi(delta(q)). The formulas define outputs on all other strings, hence give a total extension. If D is empty the identity uses only wires.
proof: As stated: shared prefix tests identify changed encoded states; each output coordinate toggles exactly when its active changed-state indicator belongs to D_j. The gate count is the sum of trie extensions, coordinate OR trees, and constant-size XOR circuits.

lemma: The current constructive lemma S0708 gives an exact extension for arbitrary sparse transitions, but its proof-state status is only CLAIMED. A further exact consequence is that for any changed set D, the trie node count T is at most S|D|, since each of the |D| codewords contributes at most S non-root prefixes; therefore S0708 recovers a O(S|D|) bound while potentially saving gates when changed encodings share prefixes. Proof: each word has exactly S prefixes of lengths 1 through S, and the trie node set is their union, so its cardinality is at most the sum S|D|. This is a general bound on the defined trie statistic; it does not establish a lower bound or close the full amortized recoding obligation.

proved_step:
statement: HAMMING-SENSITIVE SPARSE TRANSITION EXTENSION. Let Q be a finite set of size m>=1, S=ceil(log2 m), psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective, and delta:Q->Q. Set D={q:delta(q)!=q}, D_j={q in D:psi(q)_j!=psi(delta(q))_j}, and let T be the number of non-root nodes in the prefix trie of {psi(q):q in D}. Define H=sum_{q in D} dist_H(psi(q),psi(delta(q))). A total extension of the encoded transition is computable by fan-in-two AND/NOT gates using O(S+T+H) gates. Proof: For each trie node, compute the conjunction testing its prefix by extending its parent conjunction with the next matching input literal; share input negations. This uses O(T+S) gates and yields each equality indicator e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] at its leaf. For each output coordinate j, OR the indicators e_q for q in D_j, using max(0,|D_j|-1) binary OR gates, and use constant 0 if D_j is empty. Set output bit j to x_j XOR that OR; XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. At an encoded unchanged state, no changed-state indicator is true, so the output is unchanged. At psi(q) for q in D, injectivity makes exactly e_q true, so coordinate j toggles exactly when psi(q)_j differs from psi(delta(q))_j. Thus the output is psi(delta(q)); the formulas define a total map on all strings. Finally, sum_j |D_j|=H by counting each changed state once for every differing coordinate. Therefore sum_j max(0,|D_j|-1)<=H, giving the claimed gate bound. For D empty, the identity map uses wires alone.
proof: The trie computes all changed-state equality indicators with shared prefix work. Each output coordinate aggregates exactly the indicators whose transition changes that coordinate, then toggles the input bit. Injectivity ensures that on a valid encoded input precisely its own indicator is active. The number of output aggregation gates is sum_j max(0,|D_j|-1), which is at most sum_j |D_j|=H. Adding the trie gates, shared input negations, and constant-cost XOR circuits gives O(S+T+H). This proves a total extension and the stated bound for every finite instance.

statement: PREFIX-TRIE BOUND. Let A be a set of t distinct binary strings of length S, and let T(A) be the number of non-root nodes in their prefix trie. Then T(A) <= sum_{d=1}^S min(t,2^d). For t>=1, this is at most t(S-floor(log2 t))+2t-2. For t=0, T(A)=0. Proof: At depth d, trie nodes correspond to distinct length-d prefixes of strings in A. There are at most t such prefixes and at most 2^d binary strings of length d, so that level has at most min(t,2^d) nodes. Summing over depths proves the first inequality. For t>=1 let k=floor(log2 t). The sum through depth k is 2^(k+1)-2 <= 2t-2; the remaining S-k levels contribute at most t each. This proves the second bound. The statement concerns trie size only and does not assume or prove a circuit lower bound.
proof: At each depth d, every trie node is a prefix of at least one member of A, giving at most t nodes, and there are only 2^d possible prefixes, giving at most 2^d nodes. Add these bounds level by level. For the explicit estimate, depths 1 through k contribute at most sum 2^d=2^(k+1)-2 <= 2t-2, while depths k+1 through S contribute at most t per level, for t(S-k). The empty set has no trie nodes.

proved_step: CYCLE-CONCATENATION TRANSITION UPPER BOUND. Let Q be an m-element set, m>=2, and let δ be a permutation of Q with c cycles. Put S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^S such that the transition ψδψ^{-1}, defined on ψ(Q), extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computed by O(S(c+1)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Order the cycles arbitrarily and concatenate their cyclic orderings into a list q_0,...,q_{m-1}; encode q_i by the S-bit binary representation of i. Let b_i be the index of δ(q_i). For every i that is not the last index of its cycle, b_i=i+1, so ordinary binary increment agrees with the required transition. Let E be the set of cycle-end indices; |E|=c. Build a total increment-modulo-2^S map I on S bits: each carry into bit j is the conjunction of the lower j bits (with the empty conjunction equal to 1), and output bit j is x_j XOR that carry. Shared prefix conjunctions and constant-size AND/NOT implementations of XOR give O(S) gates. For each i∈E, compute e_i(x)=[x=i] by an S-literal conjunction. For output bit j, set F_j(x)=I_j(x) XOR OR_{i∈E : (i+1 mod 2^S)_j != b_i,j} e_i(x). OR trees use O(c) gates per bit, so all corrections use O(Sc) gates; equality tests use O(Sc) gates as well. At a valid non-end code i the correction is zero and I(i)=i+1=b_i. At a valid end code i, injectivity makes exactly e_i active, toggling precisely the bits where I(i) differs from b_i; hence F(i)=b_i. The formulas define F on unused codes too, giving a total extension. Therefore the circuit size is O(S(c+1)). The finite verification cm-fc5355a099b84193 checked the cycle-concatenation identity on 362,879 transitions through m=8; it is sanity evidence only, while the argument above proves the stated bound.

FEW-DISTINCT-CYCLE-LENGTH ENCODING LEMMA. For every m>=2 and every permutation delta on an m-element set Q with exactly d distinct cycle lengths l_1,...,l_d, there is an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), such that psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map computed by O(d log m + log m * sum_{i=1}^d log(l_i+1)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: For each i, list the c_i cycles of length l_i, and assign their states consecutive integer codes A_i+a*l_i+j, where A_i=sum_{h<i}c_h*l_h, 0<=a<c_i, 0<=j<l_i. These codes partition 0,...,m-1, hence their S-bit binary encodings are injective. On each such cycle delta sends x to x+1 unless j=l_i-1, in which case it sends x to x-l_i+1. For each i make an interval indicator I_i(x) for A_i<=x<A_i+c_i*l_i; binary comparison to constants costs O(log m) fan-in-two gates. Within that interval the boundary indicator is E_i(x)=[(x-A_i+1) mod l_i=0]. Compute it by subtracting the constant A_i, then scanning the resulting O(log m)-bit string from most significant to least significant while maintaining a remainder r in {0,...,l_i-1}; each bit updates r to (2r+b) mod l_i using O(log(l_i+1)) Boolean gates, so this test costs O(log m log(l_i+1)). The flags I_i AND E_i are disjoint. The ordinary output is x+1; when flag i holds, select x-l_i+1 instead. Binary increment, constant subtraction, and d-way disjoint selection cost O(d log m) gates total. Thus on every valid code the output is exactly the next state on its cycle. The same circuit defines outputs on unused codes, giving a total extension. This is a constructive bound for the stated family only; it does not prove the unrestricted O(sqrt(m) log^2 m) upper bound or any lower bound.

INTERVAL-ENCODING LEMMA. Let Q be an m-element set, m>=2, and let delta be a permutation of Q with d cycles. Put S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that the transition on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map of fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit size O((d+1)S). Proof: List the cycles in any order, with lengths ell_1,...,ell_d, and let a_i=sum_{h<i} ell_h. Enumerate cycle i as q_{i,0},...,q_{i,ell_i-1}, and encode q_{i,j} by the S-bit binary representation of a_i+j. These are distinct codes in [0,m-1], so psi is injective. Let B(x)=x+1 mod 2^S, computed by a shared ripple incrementer using O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates: the carry into bit j is the conjunction of lower bits, and XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. For each cycle endpoint e_i=a_i+ell_i-1, compute the indicator E_i(x)=[x=e_i] using an S-literal conjunction, costing O(S). On endpoint e_i, the base output B(e_i) must be changed to a_i. For each output bit r define F_r(x)=B_r(x) XOR OR_{i: B(e_i)_r differs from (a_i)_r} E_i(x). The endpoint indicators are mutually exclusive because the e_i are distinct; OR and XOR each have constant-size fan-in-two AND/NOT implementations per operation. Thus all endpoint tests and corrections cost O(dS), and the total circuit costs O((d+1)S). At a non-endpoint encoded state a_i+j with j<ell_i-1, no E_i is active and B outputs a_i+j+1, the next cycle state. At endpoint e_i exactly E_i is active and the correction changes B(e_i) to a_i, the cycle successor. This includes e_i=m-1, whether or not m is a power of two, since B is explicitly modulo 2^S. The formulas define outputs on every S-bit input, giving a total extension. This proves only an upper bound depending on the number of cycles; it does not establish a uniform O(sqrt(m) polylog(m)) bound for arbitrary permutations.

statement: GENERAL DNF EXTENSION BOUND. For every m>=1, every m-element set Q, every permutation delta:Q->Q, and S=ceil(log2 m), there exists an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computed by O(mS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Choose m distinct S-bit strings a_q and encode q by a_q. For each output coordinate j, define F_j(x)=OR_{q: (psi(delta(q)))_j=1} [x=a_q], where [x=a_q] is the conjunction of the S literals matching a_q. Implement each equality with fan-in-two AND gates, sharing input negations across all terms, and each disjunction with fan-in-two OR gates; OR is implementable with constant-size AND/NOT circuitry. Across S output bits this uses O(mS) gates. At x=a_q, exactly the q equality indicator is true, so F_j(a_q)=(psi(delta(q)))_j for every j. The formulas define a total map on all strings, including unused codes. For m=1, S=0 and the unique map needs no gates.

CANDIDATE REPAIR — grouped-length interval encoding. Let a permutation on m states have d distinct cycle lengths. Set S=ceil(log2 m), order the cycles by length, and assign each cycle of length ℓ its own consecutive interval of ℓ integers, with all cycles of the same length in one contiguous block beginning at a. On a valid code x in that block, the transition is x+1 unless (x-a+1) mod ℓ=0, in which case it is x+1−ℓ. Proof: write x=a+uℓ+r with 0≤r<ℓ and u the cycle index in the block. If r<ℓ−1 then x+1=a+uℓ+(r+1), the next state in that cycle. If r=ℓ−1 then x+1−ℓ=a+uℓ, the first state of that same cycle. The endpoint predicate is equivalent to r=ℓ−1. This proves the transition identity on every encoded state. This claim is only the arithmetic transition identity; it does not assert a circuit-size bound.

statement: CYCLE-BOUNDARY EXTENSION LEMMA. For every m>=2 and every permutation delta on an m-element set with c cycles, there is an injective encoding into S=ceil(log2 m) bits such that its transition extends to a total Boolean map with O(S(c+1)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: list states cycle by cycle in transition order and encode them as 0,...,m-1. Use B(x)=x+1 modulo 2^S as the default transition. For each cycle terminal i with start a(i), compute h_i(x)=[x=i] using S literals. Output bit j is B_j(x) XOR the OR of h_i(x) over terminal indices with B_j(i) != a(i)_j. The incrementer costs O(S); equality indicators cost O(cS); all per-bit OR and XOR corrections cost O(cS). On each valid nonterminal index, B increments to its successor. At a terminal index, exactly its equality indicator is active and the corrections produce the cycle's start code. The circuit formulas define values on unused codes too, giving a total extension.

proved_step: Universal extension upper bound for a fixed encoding. Let m≥2, S=ceil(log2 m), Q be an m-element set, ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be any injection, and δ:Q→Q be any map. Then ψ∘δ∘ψ⁻¹ on ψ(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map with at most S + m(S−1) + 3S(m−1) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and wires free. Proof: For each q∈Q, form e_q(x)=[x=ψ(q)] by ANDing its S matching literals using S−1 gates; share the S negated input bits. For output bit j, let I_j={q∈Q : ψ(δ(q))_j=1}. Define F_j(x)=OR_{q∈I_j} e_q(x), taking an empty OR as 0. A binary OR is implemented as NOT(AND(NOT a,NOT b)), at most three gates, so all output ORs use at most 3S(m−1) gates. On any encoded input ψ(q), injectivity makes e_q=1 and all other indicators 0; hence F_j(ψ(q))=ψ(δ(q))_j. On unused inputs every indicator is 0, so the circuit is a total extension (with output 0 there). Thus the stated gate count holds and is O(m log m). This is an upper bound for a fixed encoding and arbitrary transition; it gives no lower bound over encodings.

evidence: Direct construction and explicit AND/NOT gate accounting. This corrects S0718's incorrect assertion that an OR costs at most three gates when NOT gates are counted. No computation or independent review is claimed.
proved_step: REPAIRED UNIVERSAL EXTENSION UPPER BOUND WITH NOT GATES COUNTED. Let m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), Q an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S any injection, and delta:Q->Q any map. Then psi delta psi^{-1} extends to a total S-bit Boolean map using at most 2mS+2S fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: Share the S input negations. For each q form e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] using S-1 AND gates, then form h_q=NOT e_q using one NOT gate. For output bit j put I_j={q: psi(delta(q))_j=1}. If I_j is empty output constant 0; otherwise output F_j=NOT(AND_{q in I_j} h_q), using |I_j|-1 AND gates and one NOT gate. At x=psi(q), injectivity gives h_q=0 and h_r=1 for r!=q, so F_j equals psi(delta(q))_j. At an unused x all e_q=0 and all h_q=1, hence every output is 0. The total is at most S + m(S-1) + m + sum_j |I_j| + S, and sum_j |I_j|<=mS, giving 2mS+2S. Thus the fixed-encoding arbitrary-transition extension bound is O(m log m), with every NOT counted. This is an upper bound only and closes no named obligation.

statement: For every m>=2, every permutation delta on an m-element set Q, and S=ceil(log2 m), there is an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi delta psi^{-1} extends to a total Boolean map on S bits with at most O(m log m) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Choose any bijection psi from Q to the first m binary strings of length S. For each q in Q form the equality indicator e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)], using S input literals and a fan-in-two AND chain, requiring at most S-1 AND gates per q, with the input negations shared across all q. For each output coordinate j, define F_j(x)=OR over q with psi(delta(q))_j=1 of e_q(x); the OR uses at most m-1 fan-in-two OR gates, and OR is expressible using NOT and AND. On each valid code psi(q), exactly e_q is 1 by injectivity, so F_j(psi(q))=psi(delta(q))_j. On unused codes every indicator vanishes, defining a total output (all zero). The total count is at most S input negations + m(S-1) equality gates + S(m-1) OR gates, which is O(mS)=O(m log m).

statement: EVEN INVOLUTION ONE-GATE RECODING LEMMA. For every even m=2p>=2 and every fixed-point-free involution delta on an m-element set Q, with S=ceil(log2 m), there exists an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi delta psi^{-1} extends to a total S-bit Boolean map using at most one NOT gate (input wires and constants free). Proof: Partition Q into its p unordered delta-pairs and enumerate the pairs by i=0,...,p-1. Let k=ceil(log2 p). Since p<=m/2, k+1<=ceil(log2 m)=S. Encode the two members of pair i as the S-bit words 0^{S-k-1} bin_k(i) 0 and 0^{S-k-1} bin_k(i) 1, where bin_k is the k-bit binary encoding (for p=1, k=0 and the empty index field is omitted). These 2p words are distinct, so psi is injective. Define the total Boolean map F on all S-bit strings by copying every bit except the final tag bit, which it negates. F uses one NOT gate and satisfies F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for each q, because delta swaps the two members of each pair while preserving its index. This includes p=1 and arbitrary even m, including non-powers of two; unused strings require no special behavior.

statement: CANDIDATE INTERVAL-ENCODING UPPER BOUND. Let δ be a permutation of an m-element set, let d be the number of distinct cycle lengths of δ, and let S=ceil(log2 m). There exists an injection ψ into {0,1}^S such that ψδψ^{-1} on ψ(Q) extends to a total Boolean map computed by O((d+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Order the cycles arbitrarily and encode their states consecutively, in cycle order, as integers 0,...,m−1. The desired transition is x↦x+1 except at each cycle endpoint e, where it maps to the start a of that cycle. Compute the ordinary S-bit increment circuit, costing O(S). For each endpoint e, compute the equality indicator I_e(x)=[x=e] as a conjunction of S literals, costing O(S), with input negations shared. For output bit j, XOR the increment bit with the parity (XOR) of those indicators I_e for which bit j of (e+1 mod 2^S) differs from bit j of a. At a valid non-endpoint, all indicators vanish and the output is x+1; at endpoint e exactly I_e is one, so the specified output bit is toggled exactly when needed. The formula defines a total map on all S-bit strings, while its values off ψ(Q) are unconstrained. There are at most d endpoints, so indicator computation and all bit corrections use O(dS) gates. Finally, if the distinct positive cycle lengths are l_1<...<l_d, then l_i≥i and sum_i l_i≤m, hence d(d+1)/2≤m and d≤sqrt(2m). Thus every permutation admits such an encoding with O(sqrt(m) log m) gates.

statement: ENDPOINT-CORRECTION CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let δ be a permutation of an m-element set Q, m≥2, with d distinct cycle lengths, and set S=⌈log₂m⌉. There is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^S for which ψδψ⁻¹ on ψ(Q) extends to a total Boolean map using O((d+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: List the cycles in any order and each cycle in its δ-order, assigning consecutive integer codes from 0. Each cycle occupies an interval [a,e], and δ acts as x↦x+1 except at its endpoint e, where the desired output is a. The codes 0,…,m−1 fit in S bits. Compute the ordinary S-bit modular increment B(x)=x+1 with O(S) gates: the carry into bit j is the conjunction of input bits 0,…,j−1 (the empty conjunction is 1), and XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. For each of the at most d cycle endpoints e, compute I_e(x)=[x=e] as a conjunction of S literals, sharing input negations, at cost O(S) gates per endpoint. For each output bit j, XOR B_j with all indicators I_e for which bit j of (e+1 mod 2^S) differs from bit j of the start a_e of e's cycle. On a valid non-endpoint code, every indicator is zero, so the output is its successor. On a valid endpoint e, exactly I_e is one, so exactly the differing bits are toggled and the output equals a_e. This defines a total map on all S-bit inputs and has O(S+dS) gates (the dS output-bit corrections and the dS equality tests dominate). If the distinct positive cycle lengths are l_1<⋯<l_d, then l_i≥i and each length occurs at least once, so m≥∑l_i≥d(d+1)/2. Hence d≤⌊(√(8m+1)−1)/2⌋, and the gate bound is O(√m log m).

proved_step: statement: COMMON-ARBITRARY-CYCLE-LENGTH LEMMA. Let m=t*l with integers t>=1 and l>=1, and let F be a permutation of an m-element set Q whose cycles all have length l. Set S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi F psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map on S bits of fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit size O((log m)^2). Proof: Index the cycles by i in {0,...,t-1} and positions by j in {0,...,l-1}, so F(i,j)=(i,(j+1) mod l). Encode (i,j) by the S-bit binary representation of x=i*l+j, which is injective since 0<=x<m<=2^S. On valid x, let r=x mod l and define y=x+1 if r<l-1, and y=x-(l-1) if r=l-1. If r<l-1, x=i*l+r, hence y=i*l+(r+1), the encoding of F(i,r). If r=l-1, x=i*l+l-1, hence y=x-(l-1)=i*l, the encoding of F(i,l-1). Thus y is always in [0,m) and the map agrees with F on every encoded state. To realize a total Boolean extension, compute r by a bit-serial remainder circuit: process the S input bits from most significant to least; at each step replace the current remainder u by (2u+b) mod l. Since 0<=u<l, this uses O(log l) gates per bit using compare/subtract circuitry, for O(S log l) gates. Compute the two candidate arithmetic expressions x+1 and x-(l-1) with ripple carry/borrow circuits of O(S) gates each, compare r with l-1 in O(log l) gates, and select the appropriate S output bits with O(S) mux gates. Total size O(S log l+S)=O((log m)^2). Define this same circuit on all S-bit inputs; behavior outside psi(Q) is arbitrary. The l=1 case is the identity and has an O(S) extension. This gives a constructive arbitrary-common-cycle-length extension of the power-of-two-cycle subclass, at exact width S.

statement: BOUNDED-DISTINCT-CYCLE-LENGTH ENCODING LEMMA. For every m>=2 and permutation F on m states whose cycles have r distinct lengths, there is an injection into {0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), such that the encoded transition extends to a total fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of size O(r*S*log m). Proof: For each cycle length ell, group its c_ell cycles in a consecutive interval of length c_ell*ell, with offset B_ell equal to the total size of shorter-length groups. Index cycles i and positions j, and encode as x=B_ell+i*ell+j. The intervals partition [0,m), so this is injective. On the interval for ell, compute q=(x-B_ell) mod ell. Output x+1 if q<ell-1 and x-(ell-1) otherwise. For x=B_ell+i*ell+j, these outputs encode (i,j+1) modulo ell, so they equal F. A remainder circuit scans the S input bits, updating u to (2u+b) mod ell; because u<ell implies 2u+b<2ell, each update uses O(log ell) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, for O(S log ell) per group. Interval tests, subtraction, comparison, addition/subtraction candidates, and output selection use O(S) gates per group. Multiplexing across r groups yields O(r*S*log m). Assign arbitrary outputs outside [0,m) to make a total extension. This bound is useful for fixed r and leaves growing r unresolved.

proved_step: statement: Support-sensitive recoding lemma. Let Q have m states, S>=1, psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and delta:Q->Q differ from the identity on exactly t states. There is a total S-bit fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit F, with constants and input wires free, using O(tS) gates, such that F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for every q in Q. Proof: Use the identity map x as a zero-gate baseline. For each moved state q construct e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] as the conjunction of S matching literals, using O(S) gates per q and shared input negations. For each output bit j let E_j be the moved states q for which psi(q)_j differs from psi(delta(q))_j. Set F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q in E_j} e_q(x). Fan-in-two AND/NOT gates implement each OR and XOR with O(|E_j|+1) gates when E_j is nonempty; when E_j is empty use the wire x_j. Across coordinates, sum_j |E_j|<=tS, and the nonempty-coordinate overhead is at most S; for t>0 this is O(tS). For t=0 use the identity wires alone. On a valid code exactly its own equality indicator is true if it is moved, so precisely the required output bits toggle; on unmoved codes all indicators vanish. The formulas define a total circuit off the code set as well.

For output bit j, let E_j be those q in E on which the baseline and target outputs differ in bit j, and define F_j=F0_j XOR OR_{q in E_j} e_q. statement: Sparse-update-from-identity lemma. Let Q be a set of m states, S>=1, and psi:Q->{0,1}^S an injection. Let delta:Q->Q agree with the identity except on a set E of t states. There is a total S-output-bit fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit F with constants and input wires free, of size O(S+tS), such that F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for every q in Q.
proof: For each q in E define e_q(x)=1 exactly when x=psi(q), implemented as the conjunction of the S literals specifying psi(q). The input-bit negations are shared, so all indicators cost O(S+tS). For each output bit j, let E_j={q in E: psi(delta(q))_j != psi(q)_j}. Set F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q in E_j} e_q(x)); an empty OR is 0. A binary OR and XOR are implementable with a constant number of AND/NOT gates per term (De Morgan for OR; XOR has a fixed constant-size AND/NOT implementation), so all output corrections cost O(sum_j |E_j|+S)=O(tS+S). On x=psi(q), injectivity implies e_q(x)=1 only for the corresponding state, and all other indicators are zero. If q is outside E no correction fires, hence F(x)=psi(q)=psi(delta(q)); if q is in E, precisely the coordinates differing between psi(q) and psi(delta(q)) are toggled. Thus the circuit has the required values on every encoded state. The formula defines a total Boolean map on all {0,1}^S, including unused codes.

The construction builds equality indicators e_q(x) for all q in Q (m indicators, each S-1 fan-in-2 AND gates using shared input negations: total m(S-1) + S = O(mS)). For each output bit j, an OR tree over indicators where psi(delta(q))_j = 1 (binary OR via AND/NOT costs 3 gates per internal node, so O(m) per coordinate, total O(mS)). XOR with x_j is O(1) per coordinate. At x = psi(q), injectivity makes exactly e_q = 1, so output is psi(delta(q)). On unused codes all indicators are 0, output is 0^S. Total O(mS) gates. This is a standard full lookup table construction; the bound is correct and tight for arbitrary delta and psi. No argument gap found.

The construction is correct. For each q in T, e_q(x) is an S-literal conjunction testing x = psi(q); with shared input negations this costs O(S|T| + S) gates. For each output coordinate j, D_j = {q in T : psi(q)_j != psi(delta(q))_j}, and |D_j| = d_j. The OR tree over d_j indicators costs 3(d_j - 1) fan-in-2 AND/NOT gates. Sum over j gives 3(sum d_j - S') where sum d_j = sum_{q in T} h_q = H, so O(H + S). XOR with x_j costs O(1) per coordinate = O(S). Total = O(S|T| + S + H + S) = O(S + S|T| + sum h_q). Correctness: at x = psi(q) for q in T, injectivity makes e_q the sole active indicator, so exactly the differing coordinates flip. At x = psi(q) for q not in T, no indicator is active, so output = x = psi(delta(q)). The formulas define a total map on all 2^S inputs. No argument gap found.

This is a restatement of S0674 with Unicode notation. The same construction and gate count analysis applies: equality indicators e_q for q in T cost O(S|T|+S); OR trees over D_j cost O(sum|D_j|+S)=O(sum h_q+S); XORs cost O(S). Total O(S + S|T| + sum h_q). Correctness follows from injectivity of psi and mutual exclusivity of e_q on psi(Q). The 'corrected' label refers to repairing an earlier unsupported O(S+sum h_q) claim by including the equality-test cost. No argument gap found.

Construction is correct: for each output bit j, the truth table on 2^S inputs has at most 2^S minterms. Each minterm is a conjunction of S literals, costing S-1 binary AND gates (sharing negated inputs). The OR of up to 2^S minterms uses 2^S-1 binary OR gates, each OR = 3 AND/NOT via De Morgan. Per output: (S-1)*minterms + 3*(2^S-1) ≤ (S+2)*2^S = O(S·2^S). For S outputs: S * O(S·2^S) = O(S^2·2^S). With S=ceil(log2 m), 2^S ≤ 2m, so O(m (log m)^2). The lemma statement initially claims O(S·2^S) total but the proof correctly derives O(S^2·2^S); the final corrected bound is valid. No argument gap.

Construction is correct: shared negations of S inputs (O(S) NOT gates). Trie of T (t distinct S-bit codes) has L non-root prefix nodes; each node's indicator = parent_indicator AND next_literal, costing 1 AND gate per node = O(L). Leaf indicators are exactly the trie leaf indicators (1 iff input matches that code). For each output j, OR of e_q over q where psi(q)_j != psi(delta(q))_j; total leaf occurrences across all outputs = H. Binary OR tree of k indicators costs 3(k-1) AND/NOT gates; XOR with x_j costs O(1). Total O(S + L + H). The lemma honestly notes L can be Theta(St) for a full trie, so this does not prove O(S+H) in general; it isolates the prefix-sharing obstacle. No argument gap.

Construction is trivially correct: the constant function F(x) = ψ(q_*) for all x ∈ {0,1}^S outputs the fixed S-bit string ψ(q_*). Each output bit is a constant (0 or 1), which by the free-constants convention costs 0 fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. The function is total and agrees with ψ∘δ∘ψ^{-1} on all ψ(q) since δ(q) = q_* for all q. No argument gap.

Mathematical verification: the one-hot encoding construction is correct for deterministic transitions delta:Q->Q (statement has typo delta:Q->{0,1}^Q). For each j, P_j={i:delta(q_i)=q_j} partitions Q, so sum|P_j|=m. Binary OR tree with |P_j|-1 internal nodes, each OR=NOT(AND(NOT,NOT)) costs 3 gates. Total gates=3*sum max(|P_j|-1,0) <= 3m. Bound 3m <= m^2+m holds for m>=1 (m=1: 0<=2; m>=2: 3m<=m^2+m). Extension correctness: at x=e_i, only x_i=1, so F_j=1 iff i in P_j iff delta(q_i)=q_j. Uses m state bits, not ceil(log2 m) as required by the model - noted as diagnostic limitation, not proof error.

Mathematical verification: same construction as S0681 with tighter bound 3m (instead of m^2+m). The statement has typo delta:Q->{0,1}^Q but proof treats delta:Q->Q. Mathematical verification: one-hot encoding psi(q_i)=e_i in {0,1}^m. For each j in delta(Q) (size r), preimage size k_j>=1, sum k_j=m. Output bit j is OR of k_j inputs, implemented as binary tree with k_j-1 OR gates, each OR=NOT(AND(NOT,NOT)) costs 3 AND/NOT gates. Total gates = 3*sum(k_j-1) = 3(m-r). For j not in delta(Q), output is constant 0 (free). At x=e_i, exactly one input is 1, so F_j=1 iff i in preimage of q_j, i.e., delta(q_i)=q_j. Correct extension. Mathematical verification: Standard minterm construction. For each q in Q, e_q(x) = AND_{i=1}^S l_{q,i}(x) where l_{q,i} = x_i if psi(q)_i=1 else NOT x_i. Computing all S input negations once (S gates, absorbed in O(mS)). Each minterm: S-1 binary AND gates, total m(S-1). For each of S output bits, OR of up to m minterms: binary tree with at most m-1 internal nodes, each OR = NOT(AND(NOT, NOT)) costs 3 AND/NOT gates, so at most 3(m-1) per output, total 3S(m-1). Sum = m(S-1) + S + 3S(m-1) = 4mS - m - 2S = O(mS). Correctness: at x=psi(q), injectivity makes e_q=1, others 0, so F_j=1 iff psi(delta(q))_j=1. Handles m=1, S=0 as zero-bit map. No error.

Mathematical verification: Same minterm construction as S0684. For each q, e_q(x) = AND of S literals matching psi(q). Input negations shared (S gates). m minterms at S-1 AND gates each = m(S-1). For each of S outputs, OR of up to m minterms via binary tree with ≤ m-1 internal nodes, each OR = NOT(AND(NOT,NOT)) costs 3 AND/NOT gates = 3S(m-1). Total = m(S-1) + S + 3S(m-1) = O(mS). Correctness: at x=psi(q), injectivity gives e_q=1, others 0, so F_j=1 iff psi(delta(q))_j=1. No error.

Mathematical verification: A={q:delta(q)!=q}, |A|=t≤m. For each q in A, e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] costs S-1 AND gates + shared negations = O(St). For each bit j, D_j={q in A: psi(q)_j≠psi(delta(q))_j}, sum_j |D_j| ≤ S|A| = St. F_j(x) = x_j XOR OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x). OR implemented as binary tree (|D_j|-1 OR gates, each OR=NOT(AND(NOT,NOT)) costs 3 gates). XOR(a,b) = (a AND NOT b) OR (NOT a AND b) costs 4 AND/NOT gates. Total gates = O(St + S + St) = O(S(t+1)). Correctness: at x=psi(q) with q fixed (q∉A), all e_q=0, F_j=x_j=psi(q)_j=psi(delta(q))_j. At x=psi(q) with q∈A, e_q=1, others 0, so F_j = x_j XOR 1 = NOT psi(q)_j if q∈D_j, else x_j. Since q∈D_j iff psi(q)_j≠psi(delta(q))_j, output equals psi(delta(q))_j. Correct. Total map defined by same formulas. No error.

Mathematical verification: Encoding psi maps state in cycle i at position k to integer a_i+k (0≤k<b_i-a_i+1). Codes used: 0..m-1 ⊆ {0,1}^S. Incrementer u(x) computes (x+1) mod 2^S using O(S) gates (ripple-carry adder with constant 1). For each cycle endpoint b_i, e_i(x)=[x=b_i] via S-literal conjunction: b_i has S-bit pattern, e_i = AND of S literals matching it; O(cS) total. For output bit j, correction at b_i: u_j XOR (e_i AND (u_j XOR (a_i)_j)). When x≠b_i, e_i=0, output=u_j(x). When x=b_i, e_i=1, output = u_j XOR (u_j XOR (a_i)_j) = (a_i)_j. Since u(b_i)=b_i+1 (or 0 if b_i=2^S-1), the correction forces output to a_i. Endpoint indicators mutually exclusive since b_i distinct. On unused codes (m..2^S-1), same formula defines total map. Gate count: incrementer O(S) + c indicators O(cS) + c*S bit corrections O(cS) = O(cS). Correct.

Mathematical verification: Identical to S0684 and S0686 - the standard minterm construction. For each q∈Q, e_q(x) = AND_{i=1}^S l_{q,i}(x) where l_{q,i} = x_i if psi(q)_i=1 else NOT x_i. Shared negations: S gates. m minterms: m(S-1) AND gates. S outputs: each OR of ≤m minterms via binary tree with ≤m-1 internal nodes, each OR=NOT(AND(NOT,NOT)) costs 3 gates → 3S(m-1). Total = m(S-1)+S+3S(m-1) = 4mS - m - 2S = O(mS). Correctness: at valid x=psi(q), injectivity gives e_q=1, others 0, so F_j=1 iff psi(delta(q))_j=1. At unused codes, all e_q=0, so F=0 (a valid total extension). Gap noted in statement is accurate: this is a baseline truth-table upper bound, does not establish the target Ω(√m/log m) lower bound or the sharper O(√m polylog m) encoding upper bound. No mathematical error.

The claim states O(S+H) gates but the proof explicitly says 'The equality tests cost O(mS)'. Constructing all m equality indicators e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] requires m(S-1) binary AND gates plus S shared negations = Theta(mS) gates. Since m can be exponentially larger than S (S=ceil(log2 m)), O(mS) is NOT O(S+H) in general (H ≤ mS, so O(mS+H) = O(mS) which is >> O(S+H) when m is large). The stated bound O(S+H) is incorrect for this construction. A correct bound would be O(mS + H) or a different construction achieving O(S+H) would need to be given.

Mathematical verification: Same minterm construction as S0684/S0686/S0689. Choose any injective psi: Q -> {0,1}^S. For each q, e_q(x) = AND of S literals matching psi(q). Shared negations: S gates. m minterms: m(S-1) AND gates. S outputs: each OR of ≤ m minterms via binary tree with ≤ m-1 internal nodes, each OR = NOT(AND(NOT,NOT)) costs 3 gates → 3S(m-1). Total = m(S-1) + S + 3S(m-1) = 4mS - m - 2S = O(mS). Correctness: at x=psi(q), injectivity gives e_q=1, others 0, so F_j=1 iff psi(delta(q))_j=1. At unused codes, all e_q=0, so F=0 (a valid total extension). No mathematical error. The statement is correct but is the same baseline O(mS) upper bound as previous steps.

Mathematical verification: Same construction as S0688 (interval encoding for c-cycle permutation). Encode states by integers 0..m-1 in cycle order. Incrementer u(x)=x+1 mod 2^S costs O(S) gates (ripple-carry adder with constant 1). r cycle endpoints: for each endpoint a, e_a(x)=[x=a] via S-literal conjunction, O(rS) total. For each output bit j, correction at endpoint a: u_j XOR (e_a AND (u_j XOR bit_j(a))). This uses XOR and AND, each with constant-size AND/NOT implementations. Total gates: incrementer O(S) + r indicators O(rS) + r*S bit corrections O(rS) = O(rS). Correctness: at non-endpoint x, e_a=0 for all a, output = u(x) = x+1 (correct within cycle). At endpoint x=a_i, e_a=1 for that endpoint, output = bit_j(a_{i+1}) where a_{i+1} is start of next cycle. On unused codes (m..2^S-1), formula defines a total map. No error. This is a verified construction achieving O(rS) for permutations with r cycles.

Mathematical verification: This is a more detailed version of S0688/S0692. Encoding: states in cycle i at position j map to integer a_i+j. Interval indicator I_i(x) = [a_i ≤ x < a_i+l_i] implemented via two threshold comparisons (x ≥ a_i and x < a_i+l_i). Each comparison scans bits MSB-to-LSB with equal-prefix and already-less flags: standard O(S) gate implementation. Endpoint equality E_i(x) = [x = b_i] via S-literal conjunction, O(S) each, total O(kS). Ripple incrementer x+1 mod 2^S: O(S) gates. Output bit r: OR over i of (I_i AND ((E_i AND bit_r(a_i)) OR (NOT E_i AND bit_r(x+1)))). Each I_i, E_i, NOT, AND, OR has constant-size AND/NOT implementations. Total cost: k interval indicators O(kS) + k endpoint equalities O(kS) + incrementer O(S) + k*S output selections O(kS) = O(kS). Correctness: For x in I_i, if x=b_i then E_i=1, output = a_i; else E_i=0, output = x+1. For x outside all intervals (unused codes), all I_i=0, output = 0. Valid encodings are exactly 0..m-1, partitioned by I_i. Correct extension. No error. This is a constructive O(kS) upper bound for permutations with k cycles.

Mathematical verification: Same construction as S0687 (SPARSE-CHANGES EXTENSION LEMMA). Let E = {psi(q) : delta(q) != q}, |E| = t. For each a in E, e_a(x) = [x=a] via S-literal conjunction. Shared negations: S gates. t indicators: t(S-1) AND gates. For each output bit j, E_j = {a in E : a_j != psi(delta(psi^{-1}(a)))_j}. h_j = OR_{a in E_j} e_a. Binary tree OR: |E_j|-1 OR gates, each OR = NOT(AND(NOT,NOT)) costs 3 gates. sum_j |E_j| <= S*t (each changed state can differ in at most S bits). Total OR gates = sum_j (|E_j|-1) <= St. XOR per output: 4 gates each, total 4S. Total = S + t(S-1) + 3St + 4S = O(S(t+1)). Correctness: at x not in E, all e_a=0, h_j=0, y_j=x_j. At x=a in E, e_a=1, others 0, so h_j=1 iff a in E_j, i.e., iff the bit must toggle. XOR gives y_j = NOT a_j = psi(delta(psi^{-1}(a)))_j. Correct. No error. This is a verified construction.

Mathematical verification: Same construction as S0688/S0692/S0693. Encode states by integers 0..m-1 with each cycle's states forming a consecutive interval in cycle order. Shared incrementer u(x)=x+1 mod 2^S costs O(S) gates. c cycle endpoints: each equality indicator e_b(x)=[x=b] via S-literal conjunction, O(cS) total. For each output bit j, E_j = {endpoint b : bit_j(b+1) != bit_j(cycle_start)}. Correction: u_j XOR OR_{b in E_j} e_b. OR implemented as binary tree (|E_j|-1 OR gates, each OR = NOT(AND(NOT,NOT)) costs 3 gates). Total OR gates = sum_j (|E_j|-1) <= cS. XOR per output: 4 gates each = 4S. Total = O(S + cS + cS + S) = O(cS). Correctness: at non-endpoint x in valid range, all e_b=0, output = u(x) = x+1 (correct). At endpoint x=b, e_b=1, output = u_j(b) XOR 1 = NOT u_j(b) if b in E_j, else u_j(b). Since b in E_j iff bit_j(b+1) != bit_j(cycle_start), output equals bit_j(cycle_start). On unused codes (m..2^S-1), formula defines a total map. No error. This is a verified O(cS) upper bound for permutations with c cycles.

The proof defines d_i = (a_i - (b_i+1)) mod 2^S (arithmetic subtraction) but uses bitwise XOR for correction: Fhat(x) = y(x) XOR (e_i(x) AND d_i). At endpoint b_i, this gives (b_i+1) XOR d_i, which equals (b_i+1) XOR (a_i - (b_i+1)), NOT a_i. Concrete counterexample: m=3, single 3-cycle, S=2. Codes: 0=00, 1=01, 2=10. a_1=0, b_1=2. d_1 = 0-3 = 1 (mod 4) = 01. At x=2 (10): y(10)=11, Fhat(10)=11 XOR 01 = 10 (2), but correct next state is 0 (00). The construction fails as written. The fix would require d_i = a_i XOR (b_i+1) (bitwise), but the proof explicitly uses arithmetic subtraction.

Verified: sparse-transition construction per map costs O(S(1+t_i)) via equality indicators and per-bit OR-of-indicators with binary OR trees. Circuit composition by wiring outputs to inputs preserves fan-in 2 and sums gate counts. Inductive correctness on psi(Q) holds because each delta_i maps Q into Q, so the intermediate state always stays in psi(Q) where the next circuit is correct. No counterexample found.
